results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:4719:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-full-speed-v2 -->\n## Motivation\n\nThe full speed run of 2026-09-12 (04:17Z\u201308:33Z) produced 9 merges and cost the owner\neight distinct classes of manual intervention, each of which is a defect of the workflow\n(`results/telemetry/owner-handoffs/2026-09-12-main.md`, the `## 2026-09-12` sections of the\nevent log, and the run summary). The owner had to restate the concurrency limits five\ntimes while ~90 worker sessions died (69 on a dead endpoint, the rest above an unmeasured\nprovider ceiling); ask repeatedly why slots were idle while every dispatched fixer was\ndying at a model-policy preflight; ask whether the project was progressing and then\ndictate the estimate format; ask why ready PRs were not merging; watch three lane-runner\nrevisions be hand-patched in `/tmp`; switch the speed tier three times by hand; and nudge\na main session whose message-delivery script auto-resumed the goal five minutes after the\nstop order.\n\nThe target state: the owner gives **one** briefing at the start of a run (keys and their\nlimits, duration or \"until my word\", speed tier, pause deadline) and afterwards receives\nonly the half-hourly one-line estimate on the estimate issue and prose progress on the\nprogress log. Everything else is an automatic mechanism, a one-file switch, or a\nself-healing loop, and every fix lives in the repository rather than in `/tmp`.\n\nDesign document: attached as the first comment on this issue, which is the brief of\nrecord; the per-item briefs land in `local/briefs/`.\n\n## Description\n\nSeven work items, disjoint file sets, each one reviewed PR closing one sub-issue of this\ntracker.\n\n1. **Owner briefing, run-mode and standing reports.** `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates\n   one `run-brief.json` and is the only writer of `watchdog/run-mode.json` and of the\n   derived cap files; `ready_report.py` answers \"ready but open, and why\" hourly on the\n   progress log; `estimate_post.py` is the single writer of the estimate issue and renders\n   exactly the two prescribed lines. The main persona gains a Standing reports section so\n   the closing report is a duty, not a pause-message dictation.\n2. **Dispatch and telemetry.** Provider failures are classified (`concurrency_limit`,\n   `endpoint_5xx`, `retries_exhausted`, `timeout`, `task_failure`, `unknown`) and recorded\n   with the endpoint, so a capacity refusal is no longer indistinguishable from a failed\n   proof; `dispatch.sh` spools its request and retries transient classes instead of dying\n   with its prompt; a branch claim stops two writers on one worktree; an owner model\n   override lives in the policy layer instead of a PATH-shim rewrite that made the session\n   registry record the wrong model; `autofix.sh` stops defaulting to a model its own\n   preflight rejects and gains the fix \u2192 CI \u2192 review loop that lived in `/tmp`.\n3. **Capacity controller.** An AIMD controller with per-endpoint health is the only writer\n   of the caps: it measures the real limit, trips to cap 0 on a 5xx endpoint, recovers\n   through a single half-open read-only probe, subtracts declared external consumers,\n   carries the measured limit into the next run, and fixes the pause/resume cap round-trip\n   (which today saves zeros and cannot be parsed back).\n4. **Operator-tools installer and owner controls.** One versioned installer deploys the\n   operator scripts with a hash manifest; one `owner-pause.sh` implements the\n   pause-within-15-minutes procedure with a backed-up crontab; one `owner-resume.sh`\n   restores from the recorded state only; one `owner-say.sh` with an explicit mode stops\n   the terminal stop order from auto-resuming the goal.\n5. **Merge daemon and lane runner, promoted.** Honest names under\n   `results/telemetry/owner-tools/`, failure markers that carry a class and a reason with\n   class-based clearing, PAR sized from the machine, the lane's full build taken through\n   the machine-wide build lock, a retirement pass for PRs already on main, and \u2014 most\n   importantly \u2014 the lane's `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` fallback push deleted.\n6. **Self-repair janitor.** One idempotent pass re-runs sessions killed by the provider,\n   repairs parked lanes through committed repair briefs, closes mechanically superseded\n   PRs, and drops stale lane state; no date globs and no filename digit filters.\n7. **Merge hygiene and build reachability.** A committed `.gitattributes` union driver for\n   the append-only telemetry logs (today the fix exists only in one host's\n   `.git/info/attributes`), asserted by `worktree-setup.sh`; and a CI reachability guard\n   that fails a PR introducing a module outside the umbrella import closure, instead of\n   letting it surface as a pre-push gate failure on every lane three hours later.\n\n## Testing\n\nEach sub-issue's PR carries its own `scripts/tests/test_*.py` under the existing\n`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` step, plus the acceptance checks listed in\nits brief. No item changes `.githooks/*`, `merge_loss_guard.py`, `checked-push.sh`, the\nseven `pr_merge.py` gates, the eigh",

### scripts/Checkdecls.lean
import Lean

open Lean

private def stringToName (s : String) : Name :=
  (s.splitOn ".").foldl
    (fun acc component =>
      match component.toNat? with
      | some n => Name.num acc n
      | none => Name.str acc component)
    Name.anonymous

private def parseDecls (contents : String) : Array (Nat × String) :=
  let lines := (contents.splitOn "\n").toArray
  let (decls, _) :=
    lines.foldl
      (fun state line =>
        let decls := state.1
        let lineNo := state.2
        let trimmed := line.trimAscii.toString
        let decls :=
          if trimmed.isEmpty || trimmed.startsWith "#" ||
              trimmed.startsWith "--" then
            decls
          else
            decls.push (lineNo, trimmed)
        (decls, lineNo + 1))
      (#[], 1)
  decls

private def missingDecls
    (env : Environment) (decls : Array (Nat × String)) :
    Array (Nat × String) :=
  decls.filter fun (_, decl) => env.find? (stringToName decl) |>.isNone

private def usage : String :=
  "Usage: lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls"

unsafe def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do
  match args with
  | [pathStr] =>
      let path := System.FilePath.mk pathStr
      unless (← path.pathExists) do
        IO.eprintln s!"File not found: {path}"
        return 1
      let contents ← IO.FS.readFile path
      let decls := parseDecls contents
      -- Import the root module to get all declarations.
      let modules := #[{ module := `MIPStarRE : Import }]
      initSearchPath (← findSysroot)
      enableInitializersExecution
      let env ← importModules modules {} (trustLevel := 1024)
      let missing := missingDecls env decls
      if missing.isEmpty then
        IO.println s!"All {decls.size} declarations from {path} resolved."
        return 0
      IO.eprintln
        s!"Missing {missing.size} declaration(s) listed in {path}:"
      for (lineNo, decl) in missing do
        IO.eprintln s!"  line {lineNo}: {decl}"
      return 1
  | _ =>
      IO.eprintln usage
      return 1

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.MainTheorem.MainFormal

/-!
# Comparator closure extractor

Computes the transitive closure of repository-local constants referenced by the
statements of one challenge's target theorems, mirroring comparator's
`runForUsedConsts` traversal (types, definition bodies, inductive constructors,
and recursor rules; theorem proof bodies are traversed for the constants they
use).  Auto-generated auxiliaries (`_proof_`, `match_`, `_autoParam`,
constructors, projections) are collapsed into their parent declarations.

The challenge is selected by `scripts/comparator/challenges/<name>.json`:

* its `targets` reach this file through the environment variable
  `MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS` (comma-separated, fully qualified).  With the
  variable unset the extractor closes the LDT main theorem, so running this
  file directly reproduces the historical single-challenge behaviour.
* its `imports` replace the `import` block above.  `check_challenge_drift.py`
  renders a copy of this file with that block substituted, because a Lean
  module header cannot be computed at elaboration time.

Output: one TSV row per declaration — name, module path, start line, end line
(`NORANGE` for compiler-generated declarations without a source range) —
consumed by `assemble_challenge.py`.  Rows are emitted in `NameSet` order,
which is deterministic; the dependency ordering (module import rank, then line
number) happens downstream in the assembler.  See README.md in this directory
for the full regeneration pipeline.
-/

open Lean

def isLocal (env : Environment) (n : Name) : Bool :=
  match env.getModuleIdxFor? n with
  | some idx => (`MIPStarRE).isPrefixOf env.header.moduleNames[idx.toNat]!
  | none => true

/-- Name tails of compiler-generated companions of an inductive/structure
declaration; occurrences are collapsed into the parent so the assembler emits
each structure's source exactly once. -/
def generatedTails : List String :=
  ["casesOn", "rec", "recOn", "brecOn", "below", "ibelow", "binductionOn",
   "noConfusion", "noConfusionType", "injEq", "sizeOf_spec",
   "mk.inj", "mk.injEq", "mk.noConfusion", "mk.sizeOf_spec"]

def canon (env : Environment) (closure : NameSet) (n : Name) : Name :=
  let s := n.toString
  let s := (s.splitOn "._proof_").head!
  let s := (s.splitOn ".match_").head!
  -- A cached sparse matcher can be reused without referencing its original
  -- parent. Emit that parent's source so elaboration creates the same matcher.
  let s := (s.splitOn "._sparseCasesOn_").head!
  let s := (s.splitOn "._autoParam").head!
  let c := s.toName
  -- collapse compiler-generated companions into their parent inductive
  let byTail := generatedTails.findSome? fun tail =>
    if s.endsWith ("." ++ tail) then
      let parent := (s.dropRight (tail.length + 1)).toName
      match env.find? parent with
      | some (.inductInfo _) => if closure.contains parent then some parent else none
      | _ => none
    else none
  match byTail with
  | some parent => parent
  | none =>
    -- collapse constructors, recursors, and projections likewise
    let structural :=
      match env.find? c with
      | some (.ctorInfo v) => some v.induct
      | some (.recInfo v) => v.all.head?
      | _ =>
        if (env.getProjectionFnInfo? c).isSome then some c.getPrefix
        else none
    match structural with
    | some parent => if closure.contains parent then parent else c
    | none => c

/-- All local constants referenced by declaration `n`.
Mirrors comparator's `runForUsedConsts`: type + value (incl. theorem proofs)
+ inductive ctors + recursor rule RHSs. -/
def refsOf (env : Environment) (n : Name) : Array Name :=
  match env.find? n with
  | some ci =>
    let fromType := ci.type.getUsedConstants
    let fromValue := match ci.value? (allowOpaque := true) with
      | some v => v.getUsedConstants
      | none => #[]
    let extra : Array Name :=
      match ci with
      | .inductInfo v => v.ctors.toArray ++ v.all.toArray
      | .ctorInfo v => #[v.induct]
      | .recInfo v => v.rules.foldl (fun acc r => (acc.push r.ctor) ++ r.rhs.getUsedConstants) #[]
      | _ => #[]
    (fromType ++ fromValue ++ extra).filter (isLocal env)
  | none => #[]

partial def collect (env : Environment) (queue : List Name) (seen : NameSet) : NameSet :=
  match queue with
  | [] => seen
  | n :: rest =>
    if seen.contains n || !isLocal env n then collect env rest seen
    else collect env ((refsOf env n).toList ++ rest) (seen.insert n)

/-- Target theorems closed when `MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS` is unset. -/
def defaultTargets : List Name := [`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal]

/-- Parse the comma-separated target list written by `challenge_config.py`. -/
def parseTargets (s : String) : List Name :=
  ((s.splitOn ",").map String.trim).filterMap fun part =>
    if part.isEmpty then none else some part.toName

def challengeTargets : IO (List Name) := do
  match ← IO.getEnv "MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS" with
  | none => return defaultTargets
  | some raw =>
    let targets := parseTargets raw
    if targets.isEmpty then
      throw (IO.userError "MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS is set but names no target")
    return targets

def runExtract : MetaM Unit := do
  let env ← getEnv
  let targets ← challengeTargets
  -- Roots are the local constants of every target's *statement*, accumulated in
  -- configuration order; the closure itself is order-independent.
  let mut roots : List Name := []
  for target in targets do
    let some ci := env.find? target | throwError "target not found: {target}"
    roots := roots ++ ci.type.getUsedConstants.toList.filter (isLocal env ·)
  let closure := collect env roots {}
  let mut canonSet : NameSet := {}
  for n in closure.toArray do
    canonSet := canonSet.insert (canon env closure n)
  -- topological ordering happens downstream in assemble_challenge.py
  -- (module import rank, then line number)
  for c in canonSet.toArray do
    let mod := match env.getModuleIdxFor? c with
      | some idx => env.header.moduleNames[idx.toNat]!
      | none => Name.anonymous
    let path := mod.toString.replace "." "/" ++ ".lean"
    match ← Lean.findDeclarationRanges? c with
    | some r => IO.println s!"{c}\t{path}\t{r.range.pos.line}\t{r.range.endPos.line}"
    | none => IO.println s!"{c}\t{path}\tNORANGE\tNORANGE"

#eval runExtract

/--
Corrected source statement of `thm:main-formal`.

Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`.

This theorem records the two-space source theorem with the confirmed large-`k`
correction `k ≥ 400 m d`.  The paper prints the weaker hypothesis `k ≥ m d`;
the missing factor `400` is documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/issue-906-main-formal-k-bound.tex`.  The additional condition
`0 < k` corrects the zero-sampling boundary where the printed error collapses
to zero; this boundary is documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/issue-422-main-formal-zero-k-boundary.tex`. -/
theorem mainFormal
    (params : Parameters)
    [FieldModel params.q]
    {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (strategy : ProjStrat params ιA ιB)
    (eps : Error)
    (hpass : strategy.lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability ≤ eps)
    (k : ℕ)
    (hk : 400 * params.m * params.d ≤ k)
    (hk0 : 0 < k) :
    ∃ G_A : ProjMeas (Polynomial params) ιA,
      ∃ G_B : ProjMeas (Polynomial params) ιB,
        ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution (Point params))
            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementA)
            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_B.toSubMeas)
            (mainFormalError params k eps) ∧
          ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution (Point params))
            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_A.toSubMeas)
            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementB)
            (mainFormalError params k eps) ∧
          ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution Unit)
            (constSubMeasFamily G_A.toSubMeas)
            (constSubMeasFamily G_B.toSubMeas)
            (mainFormalError params k eps) := by
  sorry

end Test
end MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- `lem:pauli-completeness`: every admissible Pauli basis test has a
value-one SPCC strategy. Blueprint `lem:pauli-completeness`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`. -/
theorem exists_spcc_value_one (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy (pauliBasisTestSymm P),
      S.IsSPCC ∧ S.toStrategy.value = 1 := by
  sorry

-- source: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:82-108
--   (MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness)
/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test.
Blueprint `lem:ld-soundness`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
theorem exists_ld_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
  sorry

-- source: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean:40-65  (MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness)
/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
raw prescribed-answer operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`. The theorem uses the
once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.

`thm:pauli`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
blueprint `def:povm-distance`.
-/
theorem pauli_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
            (∀ W : PauliKind,
              rawPauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
            (∀ W : PauliKind,
              rawPauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
  sorry

-- source: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean:411-436  (MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit)
/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
coordinates. Blueprint `cor:pauli-binary`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.

The theorem assumes a nonnegative error parameter, as in the source, and uses
only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension.

**Proof dependency:** The coordinate change and all three error identities are
proved, and the source theorem `pauli_soundness` is proved as well, so this
corollary is complete: its axiom closure is `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`. The composition that closed `pauli_soundness` is recorded in
issue #614, under the umbrella issue #529. -/
theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,

                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
            (∀ W : PauliKind,
              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
            ∀ W : PauliKind,

                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by

-- source: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:82-108
--   (MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness)
/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test.
Blueprint `lem:ld-soundness`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
theorem exists_ld_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron
                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
                (fun u outcome =>
                  heteroKron 1
                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
  sorry

    def ns_stack_at(self, path: str, line_no: int) -> list[str]:
        """Namespace stack (list of names) active just before 1-indexed line_no."""
        stack: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []

class SplitAssembler(Assembler):
    """Emit one Mathlib-only challenge module per contributing library module.

    Lean caches an abstracted nested proof and a `match` auxiliary *per module*,
    keyed by the statement and named after the first declaration of that module
    that needs it, and a module only sees the instances its imports declare.  A
    single-file challenge therefore cannot reproduce either name when a library
    fact is needed in two library modules, and it makes every instance visible
    to every declaration.  Mirroring the library's module partition and import
    graph reproduces both by construction.
    """

    def module_body(self, path: str, entries: list[Entry]) -> str:
        self.out = []
        self.cur_ns = []
        self.open_prelude = None
        return self.emit(entries, [])


def minimal_mirror_imports(
    asm: SplitAssembler, path: str, contributing: set[str]
) -> list[str]:
    """Contributing modules `path` imports, with redundant ancestors dropped."""
    reach = {q for q in asm.local_closure(path) if q in contributing}
    minimal = [
        q
        for q in reach
        if not any(r != q and q in asm.local_closure(r) for r in reach)
    ]
    return sorted(minimal)

basis, the construction multiplies by the inversion-invariant square root of
the transition element to the trace-dual basis in the group algebra. This is
the construction underlying `exists_selfDualNormalBasis`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:702-725`. -/
theorem exists_self_dual_normal_basis_gal (hodd : Odd (Nat.card G)) :
    ∃ c : Module.Basis G (ZMod 2) K,
      (∀ σ τ, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (c σ * c τ) =
        if σ = τ then 1 else 0) ∧
      ∃ α : K, ∀ σ, c σ = σ α := by
  classical
  let A := MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G
  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
  let φ : A ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] K :=
    (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
  let ψ : A ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] K :=
    (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
  let v : A := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
  let invAlg : A ≃ₐ[ZMod 2] A :=
    MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (MulEquiv.inv G)
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := (monoid_algebra_sq_bijective hodd).surjective v
  change u ^ 2 = v at hu
  have hv_unit : IsUnit v := normal_basis_transition_is_unit
  have hu_unit : IsUnit u := by
    rw [← isUnit_pow_iff (by omega : 2 ≠ 0), hu]
    exact hv_unit
  let U : Aˣ := hu_unit.unit
  have hU : (U : A) = u := hu_unit.unit_spec
  have hu_inv : invAlg u = u := by
    apply (monoid_algebra_sq_bijective hodd).injective
    calc
      invAlg u ^ 2 = invAlg (u ^ 2) := (map_pow invAlg u 2).symm
      _ = invAlg v := congrArg invAlg hu
      _ = v := normal_basis_transition_inv
      _ = u ^ 2 := hu.symm
  let mulU : A ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] A := Units.mulLeftLinearEquiv (ZMod 2) A U
  let c : Module.Basis G (ZMod 2) K :=
    (MonoidAlgebra.basis G (ZMod 2)).map (mulU.trans φ)
  have hc (σ : G) :
      c σ = φ ((U : A) * MonoidAlgebra.single σ (1 : ZMod 2)) := by
    simp only [c, Module.Basis.map_apply, LinearEquiv.trans_apply,
      MonoidAlgebra.basis_apply]
    exact congrArg φ (Units.mulLeftLinearEquiv_apply (ZMod 2) U _)
  have htransition (a : A) : φ (v * a) = ψ a := normal_basis_transition a
  have hc_dual (τ : G) :
      c τ = ψ ((U⁻¹ : Aˣ) * MonoidAlgebra.single τ (1 : ZMod 2)) := by
    rw [hc, ← htransition]
    apply congrArg φ
    rw [← hu, ← hU]
    symm
    calc
      (U : A) ^ 2 * ((U⁻¹ : Aˣ) * MonoidAlgebra.single τ (1 : ZMod 2)) =
          (U : A) * (((U : A) * (U⁻¹ : Aˣ)) *
            MonoidAlgebra.single τ (1 : ZMod 2)) := by
              simp only [pow_two, mul_assoc]
      _ = (U : A) * MonoidAlgebra.single τ (1 : ZMod 2) := by simp
  refine ⟨c, ?_, φ (U : A), ?_⟩
  · intro σ τ
    rw [hc σ, hc_dual τ, trace_group_algebra_pairing]
    have hInvU : invAlg (U : A) = (U : A) := by simpa [hU] using hu_inv
    rw [map_mul, hInvU, MonoidAlgebra.domCongr_single]
    simp only [MulEquiv.inv_apply]
    by_cases h : σ = τ
    · subst τ
      simp [mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm]
    · have hne : σ⁻¹ * τ ≠ 1 := by simpa [inv_mul_eq_one]
      have hne' : τ * σ⁻¹ ≠ 1 := by simpa [mul_comm] using hne
      simp [mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, h, hne']
  · intro σ
    rw [hc, normal_basis_repr_symm_mul_single]
    simp only [one_smul]
    rfl

end NormalTraceDual

/-- Existence over the binary extension of cardinality `2^k` for odd `k`;
blueprint `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`,
paper `04_preliminaries.tex:702-725`. -/
theorem exists_selfDualNormalBasis {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] (k : ℕ) (hk : Odd k)
    (hcard : Fintype.card K = 2 ^ k) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin k) (ZMod 2) K,
      Basis.IsSelfDual b ∧ Basis.IsNormal b := by
  classical
  let G := Gal(K/(ZMod 2))
  letI : CommGroup G := IsCyclic.commGroup
  have hfinrank : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) K = k := by
    apply Nat.pow_right_injective (by omega : 1 < 2)
    change 2 ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) K = 2 ^ k
    calc
      2 ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) K =
          Fintype.card (ZMod 2) ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) K := by norm_num
      _ = Fintype.card K := Module.card_eq_pow_finrank.symm
      _ = 2 ^ k := hcard
  have hcardG : Nat.card G = k :=
    (IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank (ZMod 2) K).trans hfinrank
  have hoddG : Odd (Nat.card G) := hcardG ▸ hk
  obtain ⟨cG, hcG_selfDual, α, hcG_normal⟩ :=
    exists_self_dual_normal_basis_gal (K := K) hoddG
  let frob := FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic (ZMod 2) K
  let e₀ : Fin (Module.finrank (ZMod 2) K) ≃ G := Equiv.ofBijective
    (fun i => frob ^ i.1)
    (FiniteField.bijective_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_pow (ZMod 2) K)
  let e : Fin k ≃ G := (finCongr hfinrank.symm).trans e₀
  let c : Module.Basis (Fin k) (ZMod 2) K := cG.reindex e.symm
  refine ⟨c, ?_, α, ?_⟩
  · intro i j
    rw [Module.Basis.reindex_apply, Module.Basis.reindex_apply]
    simpa [e] using hcG_selfDual (e i) (e j)
  · intro i
    rw [Module.Basis.reindex_apply, hcG_normal]
    change (frob ^ i.1) α = α ^ (Fintype.card (ZMod 2) ^ i.1)
    rw [AlgEquiv.coe_pow,
      FiniteField.coe_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_iterate]

theorem zmod2_fin_equiv_symm_val (x : ZMod 2) :
    ((ZMod.finEquiv 2).symm x).val = if x = 1 then 1 else 0 := by
  fin_cases x <;> rfl

/--
A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for blueprint
`def:binary-representation`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
-/
/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
  basisDim : ℕ
  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
  over the binary field. -/
  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
  /--
  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
  coordinate clause of blueprint
  `def:binary-representation`, with paper origin
  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
  -/
  representation_natural :
    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
    if i = j then 1 else 0
  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)

/-!
The paper fixes the field representation and self-dual normal basis once for
each admissible field size.  We expose that choice through a single global
selector rather than carrying a potentially different model in every game
parameter record.  Existence is a named stage-4.3 proof obligation; the
selector itself is the resulting noncomputable choice.
-/

/-- An admissible binary field size admits the fixed self-dual normal model used
by the Pauli basis test.  This is the existence assertion implicit in
`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis` and blueprint
`def:binary-representation`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680,702-725`.

This theorem constructs the finite field and its little-endian coordinate
coding.  It records only mathematical existence; it does not formalize the
algorithmic complexity assertion in `lem:efficient_basis`.
-/
theorem exists_fixed_field_model (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    Nonempty (FixedFieldModel q) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hq⟩ := hq
  subst q
  have hk0 : k ≠ 0 := by
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hk
    omega
  letI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  let K := GaloisField 2 k
  letI : Fintype K := Fintype.ofFinite K
  have hcardK : Fintype.card K = 2 ^ k := by
    rw [Fintype.card_eq_nat_card, GaloisField.card 2 k hk0]
  obtain ⟨b, hb_selfDual, hb_normal⟩ :=
    exists_selfDualNormalBasis (K := K) k hk hcardK
  let bitEquiv : (Fin k → ZMod 2) ≃ (Fin k → Fin 2) :=
    Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ => (ZMod.finEquiv 2).symm
  let fieldEquiv : K ≃ Fin (2 ^ k) :=
    b.equivFun.toEquiv |>.trans bitEquiv |>.trans finFunctionFinEquiv
  refine ⟨{
    toFieldModel := {
      K := K
      instField := inferInstance
      instFintype := inferInstance
      instDecidableEq := inferInstance
      equiv := fieldEquiv
    }
    algebra := (inferInstance : Algebra (ZMod 2) K)
    basisDim := k
    basisDimOdd := hk
    basisCard := rfl
    basis := b
    representation_natural := ?_
    selfDual := hb_selfDual
    normal := ?_
  }⟩
  · intro v
    change (fieldEquiv (b.equivFun.symm v)).val = _
    simp only [fieldEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_toEquiv,
      LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, bitEquiv]
    rw [finFunctionFinEquiv_apply]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    change ((ZMod.finEquiv 2).symm (v i)).val * 2 ^ i.1 = _
    rw [zmod2_fin_equiv_symm_val]
    split_ifs <;> simp
  · obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := hb_normal
    refine ⟨α, fun i => ?_⟩
    simpa using hα i

/-- The once-and-for-all field model selected for an admissible size.  Every
QPBT parameter record uses this same choice, matching the paper's fixed
self-dual normal-basis identification rather than quantifying over arbitrary
representations.  Blueprint `def:binary-representation`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`.
-/
noncomputable def fixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) (hq : IsAdmissibleSize q) :
    FixedFieldModel q :=
  Classical.choice (exists_fixed_field_model q hq)

instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Field F.K := F.toFieldModel.instField
instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Fintype F.K := F.toFieldModel.instFintype
instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : DecidableEq F.K := F.toFieldModel.instDecidableEq
instance {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : Algebra (ZMod 2) F.K := F.algebra

/-- The fixed binary representation obtained from the chosen basis coordinates. -/
noncomputable def binaryRepresentation {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K ≃ Fin q :=
  F.toFieldModel.equiv

/--
The coordinate map associated with a finite basis.  This is the `κ` of
blueprint `def:subfields-kappa`,
whose paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502`.
-/
noncomputable abbrev kappa {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Semiring K]
    [Algebra F K] [Finite ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K ≃ₗ[F] (ι → F) :=
  b.equivFun

/--
Multiplication by `a` in basis coordinates, using Mathlib's
`Algebra.leftMulMatrix`.  It is the multiplication table `K_a` in blueprint
`def:subfields-kappa`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.
-/
noncomputable abbrev multiplicationTable {F K ι : Type*} [CommSemiring F]
    [Semiring K] [Algebra F K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : K →ₐ[F] Matrix ι ι F :=
  Algebra.leftMulMatrix b

/--
The finite-field trace used by the Pauli phases.  This is a thin wrapper around
Mathlib's basis-independent `Algebra.trace`, matching Equation `eq:def-trace`
in blueprint `def:subfield-trace`
(`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`).
-/
noncomputable abbrev binTrace (K : Type*) [CommRing K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] :
    K →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2 :=
  Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K

/-- The trace selected by a fixed model; this is the map denoted `tr` in the
paper's blueprint `def:binary-representation`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`. -/
noncomputable def fixedBinTrace {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K → ZMod 2 :=
  binTrace F.K

/--
The matrix-trace presentation of `fixedBinTrace`, a statement-level bridge to
Equation `eq:def-trace`.  It is the trace assertion in blueprint
`def:subfield-trace`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.  Mathlib's
`Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` supplies the basis-independent equality.
-/
theorem fixedBinTrace_eq_matrixTrace {q ι : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin ι) (ZMod 2) F.K) (a : F.K) :
    fixedBinTrace F a = (multiplicationTable b a).trace := by
  exact Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace b a

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
/-- Prime-power metadata extracted from `params.hqPrimePower`, exposing the
honest finite-field carrier `GaloisField p n` underlying the paper's notation
`F_q`. -/
structure PrimePowerFieldSpec (params : Parameters) where
  p : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  pPrime : Nat.Prime p
  nPos : 0 < n
  cardEq : params.q = p ^ n

/-- Recover the prime-power specification bundled inside `Parameters`. -/
noncomputable def Parameters.primePowerFieldSpec
    (params : Parameters) : PrimePowerFieldSpec params :=
  have : Nonempty (PrimePowerFieldSpec params) := by
    obtain ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ := params.hqPrimePower
    exact ⟨{
      p := p
      n := n
      pPrime := hp
      nPos := hn
      cardEq := hq
    }⟩
  this.some

/-- An honest finite field of order `q`, obtained from the prime-power
witness bundled in `Parameters`. -/
noncomputable abbrev HonestFq (params : Parameters) (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params) :=
  letI : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
  GaloisField spec.p spec.n

/-- A bundled field model for the paper's `F_q`, together with a coding equivalence
to the repository's finite carrier `Fin q`. -/
class FieldModel (q : ℕ) where
  K : Type*
  instField : Field K
  instFintype : Fintype K
  instDecidableEq : DecidableEq K
  equiv : K ≃ Fin q

attribute [instance_reducible, instance] FieldModel.instField FieldModel.instFintype
  FieldModel.instDecidableEq

namespace FieldModel

/-- The carrier bundled in a `FieldModel q` has exactly `q` elements, matching the
paper's finite-field convention `|F_q| = q` (`preliminaries.tex`, lines 17--19). -/
@[simp] theorem card (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
    Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) = q := by
  simpa using Fintype.card_congr (FieldModel.equiv (q := q))

/-- A bundled field model has a nonempty finite carrier. -/
theorem card_pos (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
    0 < Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) :=
  Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨0⟩

/-- The finite cardinality of a bundled field model is nonzero. -/
theorem card_ne_zero (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
    Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) ≠ 0 :=
  Nat.ne_of_gt (card_pos q)

end FieldModel

/-- Build the honest field model from prime-power data. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def PrimePowerFieldSpec.toFieldModel (params : Parameters)
    (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params) : FieldModel params.q := by
  classical
  letI : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
  let K := HonestFq params spec
  letI : Fintype K := Fintype.ofFinite K
  have hcard : Fintype.card K = params.q := by
    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, spec.cardEq]
    simpa [K, HonestFq] using (GaloisField.card (p := spec.p) (n := spec.n) spec.nPos.ne')
  exact
    { K := K
      instField := inferInstance
      instFintype := inferInstance
      instDecidableEq := inferInstance
      equiv := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard }

/-- The canonical field model associated to the paper-faithful prime-power data
stored in `params`. Lean prefers larger numeric priorities, so this fallback
uses `100` while the `params.next` transport below uses `200`; that lets
instance search reuse an already chosen model when one is available. This
instance is noncomputable because the coding equivalence to `Fin q` is obtained
from finite cardinality data, so declarations that discover it through
typeclass search may also need to be marked `noncomputable` when they reduce
the model. -/
noncomputable instance (priority := 100) (params : Parameters) : FieldModel params.q :=
  PrimePowerFieldSpec.toFieldModel params (Parameters.primePowerFieldSpec params)

/-- Reuse an already chosen field model for successor parameters. Since Lean
prefers larger numeric priorities, this transport uses `200` so it is tried
before the canonical fallback above. -/
instance (priority := 200) {params : Parameters} [inst : FieldModel params.q] :
    FieldModel params.next.q := by
  simpa [Parameters.next] using inst

abbrev Scalar (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] := FieldModel.K params.q
abbrev PolynomialModel (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :=
  MvPolynomial (Fin params.m) (Scalar params)
abbrev LinePolynomialModel (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :=

The comparison was made against the local\nMathlib checkout by inspecting\n\n```bash\ngit -C .lake/packages/mathlib diff --name-status v4.30.0-rc2..v4.31.0\ngit -C .lake/packages/mathlib log --oneline v4.30.0-rc2..v4.31.0 -- <area>\n```\n\nwhere `<area>` ranged over the matrix, finite-sum, probability,\nmultivariate-polynomial, finite-field, convexity, and C*-algebra directories\nused by the LDT formalization.\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThe upgrade is expected to be mostly an API and import-move upgrade rather than\na mathematical restatement of the project. Before\\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\\n\\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\\nmathematically load-bearing.\\n\\nReviewers should also inspect `\\\\lean{}` and `\\\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\\n\\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\\n\\n### Companion document\\n\\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\\n\\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\\n\\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\\n`AGENTS.md`):\\n\\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\\n> conditional helper\\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\\n\\n### Axiom policy\\n\\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\\nthe axiomatic base.\\n\\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\\nfaithful to the paper.\\n\\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\n\\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\\n\\nSigns to watch for:\\n\\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib versions\\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\\n  semantics (e.g., a \\\"projective measurement\\\" definition that does not enforce\\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\\n- Definitions that \\\"work\\\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\\n  incompatible universes)\\n\\nWhen reviewing If the\\nbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\\nto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\\ntracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\\n\\nNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift. Complements\\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\\nbake in*.\\n\\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\\n\\n## Why this matters\\n\\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\\n\\n- Be marked `\\\\leanok` in the blueprint,\\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\\n\\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\\ncodebase.\\n\\n## Catalogue\\n\\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\\n\\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\\nPR [#491].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\\\leanok` tag\\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\\n  conclusion.\\n- The proof body is one of:\\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\\n\\n```lean\\ntheorem mainInduction\\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\\n```\\n\\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\\n\\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\\nthe preferred shape for new work.\\n\\nA signature passes the smell test if:\\n\\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\\n\\n### Related issues and patterns\\n\\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\\n\\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \\\"mathematical\\ncontent\\\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\\nissues [#477], [#494].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \\\"proof\\\" transports none of the\\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\\nanywhere in Lean.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\\n  directly.\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\\n\\n```lean\\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\\n\\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\\n    (α β : Point params) :\\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\\n\\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\\n  · intro α β\\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\\n  ...\\n```\\n\\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\\ndefinition equals itself.\\n\\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\\n\\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\\n   concrete objects.\\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\\n\\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \\\"precondition not met.\\\" Downstream\\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \\\"the output\\\" is\\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\\nprecondition failed.\\n\\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\\n\\\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\\\" The Lean should\\nmatch.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\\n\\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\\n\\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\\n\\n```lean\\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\\n  match g with\\n  | some p => p.poly\\n  | none   => 0\\n```\\n\\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\\n\\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\\nare visible at call sites.\\n\\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\\n\\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \\\"the output satisfies\\nP\\\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\\nsmuggling a precondition.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nPick one of:\\n\\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\\n   be passed.\\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\\n   the case, so theorems about \\\"the output\\\" now quantify only over the\\n   `some` branch.\\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\\n\\n### Classical-logic dependencies\\n\\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\\n#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\\nThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\\nnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\\nbottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of\\nclassical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#307] — placeholder Lagrange coefficient (original fallback tracker)\\n- [#495] — the full pasting-interpolation catalogue\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials\\n\\n**Smell.** A theorem of the shape `∃ x, P x` is closed by picking\\n`x := default`, `x := 0`, `x := 1`, or `x := Classical.arbitrary`, where the\\npaper names a *specific, non-trivial* `x` and derives `P x` from real\\nstructure. The Lean claim is *mathematically* weaker because the Lean\\ntheorem guarantees less than the paper's (it proves some-trivial-thing, not\\nthe-specific-paper-thing). See [#449] for the full ledger.\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\nThe theorem name matches a paper lemma but the witness has been cheapened\\ninto a placeholder. Downstream theorems that inspect the witness get `0` or\\n`default`, which is almost always useless. Consumers that \\\"use\\\" the lemma\\nare really using the trivial `∃` and cannot proceed past the first attempt\\nto pin the witness down.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `refine ⟨default, ?_⟩` / `exact ⟨default, ...⟩` / `refine ⟨0, ?_⟩` /\\n  `exact ⟨1, ...⟩` inside a proof of a paper-cited existential.\\n- `letI : Inhabited X := ⟨Classical.arbitrary X⟩` followed by a `let x :=\\n  default`.\\n- `Classical.arbitrary` / `Classical.choice` / `Nonempty.some` in proof\\n  bodies (as opposed to typeclass definitions).\\n- Identifier suffix `...Witness := default` on a bundled output.\\n\\n### Concrete example\\n\\nFrom the ledger in [#449]:\\n\\n- `lem:sdp` / `sdp` — primal witness is `T := default` (a zero\\n  submeasurement) and dual witness `Z := 1`. The paper requires a specific\\n  feasible pair; the Lean version proves only that some arbitrary pair exists,\\n  which always does.\\n- `lem:projective-low-rank-sum` / `projectiveLowRankSum` — auxiliary\\n  projective measurement `t := (default : ProjMeas Outcome ι)`. The paper\\n  constructs `(auxSpace, T_a)` from the eigenvector basis of each rounded\\n  `R_a`; the Lean version picks a zero-dimensional placeholder, which is\\n  disconnected from the paper's SVD derivation.\\n- ~~`lem:global-rewrite` / `globalRewrite` — decomposition witness is\\n  `default`~~ (historical; resolved by PRs #527 and #542). The live theorem now\\n  uses `canonicalGlobalVarianceDecomposition`, and\\n  `globalVarianceTraceWitness` consumes the centered residual family\\n  `u ↦ A^u - A_{\\\\mathrm{avg}}` rather than ignoring the witness.\\n\\n### Acceptable uses\\n\\nNon-computable instances required for typeclass plumbing, such as\\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)` inhabited by the zero polynomial, are fine when\\nthey are used only to *inhabit* a type, not to discharge a paper-cited\\nexistential.  Degenerate measurements should be constructed explicitly with a\\nspecified outcome rather than supplied by an ambient `Inhabited` instance.  The\\nsmell is specifically about `default` showing up in the proof of a *theorem\\nnamed after a paper result*.\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\n- Construct the paper's witness explicitly. If the ingredients are not yet\\n  formalized (e.g., Mathlib SVD, spectral decomposition), extract a bridge\\n  lemma that *constructs* the witness from the missing Mathlib facts, and\\n  track the Mathlib gap as a separate issue.\\n- Keep the existential statement, but strengthen the conclusion so that\\n  `x := default` no longer satisfies it (e.g., \\\"there exists `x` *with*\\n  rank `m`\\\", not merely \\\"there exists `x`\\\").\\n- If the witness cannot yet be constructed, keep the source-facing existential\\n  statement and expose the missing construction as a named proof obligation.\\n  Replacing `default` by an explicit bridge hypothesis is still an A1-grade\\n  placeholder, not a proof of the paper theorem.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#449] — master ledger; all three known cases are already listed\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib\\n\\n**Smell.** Lean code re-declares or re-proves something that already lives\\nin Mathlib, or builds a tower of custom lemmas that never bottom out in\\nMathlib / Lean core. The proof \\\"works\\\" only because the internal custom\\nstatements are compatible with each other — it is a closed ecosystem that\\ndoesn't ground in the reference library.\\n\\nThis is the \\\"scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\\" section of\\n[`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md) in concrete examples. The two\\nflavours:\\n\\n1. **Re-proving Mathlib.** Writing `private lemma my_add_comm : a + b = b + a`\\n   when `add_comm` exists.\\n2. **Custom types that shadow Mathlib.** Defining `MyMeasurement` instead of\\n   using `MeasureTheory.Measure`, `MyMatrix` instead of `Matrix`,\\n   `MyHermitian` instead of `Matrix.IsHermitian`. The custom version may be\\n   definitionally equal to (or coercible from) the Mathlib version, but if\\n   it isn't, every consumer must reprove everything.\\n\\n### Why it's bad\\n\\n1. The duplicated statements aren't audited by Mathlib's community, so they\\n   may be subtly wrong (wrong edge case, wrong universe, wrong typeclass).\\n2. When the real Mathlib proof is needed (for a key gap lemma), the custom\\n   tower must be rewritten to interoperate — often via a painful coercion\\n   layer that reintroduces every fact.\\n3. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because \\\"our\\n   version is simpler,\\\" the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\n- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis\\n  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).\\n- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a\\n  standard concept.\\n- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib\\n  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.\\n- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`\\n  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,\\n  analysis, measure theory).\\n\\n### How to fix it\\n\\nBefore writing a new lemma, spend one minute on:\\n\\n- `exact?` / `apply?` on the goal.\\n- `#find` / `Loogle` for the statement shape.\\n- `rg -n \\\"theorem.*X\\\" .lake/packages/mathlib/` for a keyword.\\n\\nIf Mathlib has it, use it. If it doesn't, consider whether the missing\\nlemma should be upstreamed (file an issue against Mathlib, or at least a\\nTODO pointing at the gap). The project already has this mandate — see the\\n\\\"Mathlib Integration\\\" section of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):\\n\\n> Scout Mathlib first (`exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source)\\n\\nA5 is what happens when that step is skipped.\\n\\n### Audit cross-reference\\n\\n`audits/` contains chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency scouting\\nreports. If a section of the code review says \\\"this could use Mathlib\\nlemma X\\\", it belongs in a specific `audits/*.md` file for that chapter.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles\\n\\n**Smell.** A theorem takes a hypothesis of type `SomeStatement` (or\\n`SomeWitness`, `SomeOutput`, etc.) that is defined elsewhere and intended\\nto represent an external mathematical result, but there is no theorem\\nconstructing it from the hypotheses under which the paper uses it. The Lean\\nstatement is then:\\n\\\"assuming the external result, the Lean conclusion holds.\\\" That is\\nsometimes legitimate (e.g., a cite to a book whose formalization we don't\\nplan to do), and sometimes a cover for locally-unwanted work.\\n\\nThis overlaps with A1 but is subtler: the hypothesis isn't the\\n*current theorem's* conclusion, it's an *independently-named* claim that\\nhappens to unblock the current proof.\\n\\n### Acceptable external smuggles\\n\\n- **Genuine external citations.** `PolishchukSpielmanClassicalSoundnessStatement`\\n  cites the Polishchuk–Spielman theorem; we don't plan to formalize it.\\n- **Mathlib gaps we can't fill.** `hMatrixChernoff` in `chernoffBernoulliMatrix`\\n  is a Mathlib matrix-Chernoff-type statement; we flagged the gap upstream.\\n- **Tracked internal obligations.** A `*Statement` that has an open sub-issue\\n  and a named construction theorem target is trackable proof debt. It is still\\n  not an acceptable extra hypothesis on a source-labelled paper theorem.\\n\\n### Unacceptable external smuggles\\n\\n- A `*Statement` with no open tracking issue, no docstring explaining the\\n  mathematical gap, and no consumer-side comment flagging the smuggle.\\n- A `*Statement` whose body is the theorem's conclusion, wearing a different\\n  name (A1 in disguise).\\n- A `*Statement` used to close a lemma whose paper version does not require\\n  any such external assumption (silent strengthening of the Lean theorem\\n  relative to the paper's).\\n\\n### How to spot it\\n\\nGrep for these suffixes: `*Statement`, `*Witness`, `*Claim`,\\n`*Conclusion`, `*Output`, `*Input`, `*Hypothesis`, `*Requirement`,\\n`*Assumption`, `*Package` (that isn't a `*BridgePackage`). For each, ask:\\n\\n- Is there a theorem anywhere that **constructs** a value of this type from the\\n  paper hypotheses?\\n- If not, is the absence explained in a docstring / tracking issue /\\n  `audits/` entry?\\n- Does the paper depend on an external theorem of this shape?\\n\\nIf any answer is \\\"no\\\", the structure is an unacceptable smuggle.\\n\\n### Current status (audited 2026-05-08)\\n\\nThe May 2026 re-audit\\n([`audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md`](../blob/main/audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md))\\nclassified 39 `*Statement` structures (102 declarations total across the\\nextended suffix sweep of `*Witness`/`*Conclusion`/`*Input`/etc.).\\n\\nThe live ledger is [#1379], replacing the now-closed [#449] (2026-05-01) and\\n[#451] (2026-04-30). Headline counts from the re-audit: 33 grounded, 2 tracked\\nsmuggle, 2 external citation, 1 paper-faithful packaging, 1 dead. Without a live\\nledger, **5 `*Statement` structures landed between 2026-04-18 and 2026-05-08\\nwithout a tracker entry** — the gap this policy fixes.\\n\\nThe Section 5 spectral-truncation chain is now an example of the preferred\\nmigration: the old `SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation has been removed, and\\nlater arguments call direct constructors for `SpectralTruncationStatement`\\ninstead of carrying an `Input` wrapper.\\n\\nIf you add a new `*Statement`-style structure to this codebase, include a\\ndef-site docstring with its paper origin (per the \\\"earn your place\\\" policy in\\n[#1379]). If no construction theorem exists yet, file a sub-issue in [#1379]\\nand ship the source-faithful construction theorem with an explicit unfinished\\nproof obligation. Do not add the structure as a new source-theorem hypothesis\\nmerely to keep downstream declarations compiling.\\n\\n### Merge gate — new `*Statement` / `*Witness` / `*Input` structures\\n\\nTo prevent dead scaffolds from landing unnoticed (the 5-structure gap of\\n2026-04-18–2026-05-08), every PR that introduces a new `structure XStatement`,\\n`structure XWitness`, `structure XInput`, `abbrev XStatement`, or\\n`abbrev XInput` must satisfy **at least one** of these before merge:\\n\\n1. **Has a construction theorem.** A theorem that constructs a value of this\\n   type from the appropriate paper hypotheses appears in the same PR or an\\n   already-merged ancestor. If the proof is not finished, the theorem must carry\\n   the explicit tracked proof obligation rather than moving the assertion into a\\n   paper-facing theorem's hypotheses.\\n2. **Has a consumer.** A theorem that takes a value of this type as a\\n   hypothesis appears in the same PR or an already-merged ancestor.\\n3. **Has a ledger entry.** A classification comment (G / E / T / P / D, per\\n   the verdict key in [#1379]) is posted on [#1379] as an issue comment, and\\n   the structure's def-site docstring links to that comment.\\n\\nStructures that satisfy none of the above are dead on arrival and must not\\nmerge.\\n\\n### Related issues\\n\\n- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces closed [#449] / [#451])\\n- [#449] — historical paper-wide gap tracker (closed 2026-05-01)\\n- [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis tracker (closed 2026-04-30)\\n- [#278] — the original \\\"derive `PermInvState` internally\\\" discussion\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Reviewer checklist\\n\\nUse this alongside the blocker\\nlist in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)\\nchecklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper\\nresult, ask:\\n\\n- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the\\n      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.\\n- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If\\n      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match\\n      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.\\n- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if\\n      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature\\n      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.\\n- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an\\n      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness\\n      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.\\n- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a\\n      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it\\n      (A5).\\n- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /\\n      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its\\n      grounding plan (A6)?\\n- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's\\n      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences\\n      as ⚠️S in [#1379].\\n\\nA lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is\\nscaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with\\n`\\\\leanok` until the gap is closed).\\n\\n## CI prevention\\n\\nMechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:\\n\\n- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use\\n  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current\\n  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses\\n  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares\\n  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers\\n  separately. When [#438] lands (`\\\\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same\\n  idea to all `\\\\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any\\n  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion\\n  structure, warn.\\n- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where\\n  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\\\\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases\\n  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in\\n  an allow-list.\\n- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,\\n  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have\\n  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.\\n- **A4 (default witnesses).** Grep `:= default`, `refine ⟨default`, `exact\\n  ⟨default`, `Classical.arbitrary` inside proof bodies (not typeclass\\n  definitions). Cross-reference to [#1379]'s witness ledger.\\n- **A5 (Mathlib bypass).** No reliable CI check, but `audits/` reports\\n  catch it during per-chapter audits.\\n- **A6 (external smuggles).** Every new `structure *Statement` without a\\n  producing theorem should be required to carry a `/-- Grounded by: #NNN\\n  -/` docstring, enforced by a lint rule over `blueprint/`.\\n\\nThe scripts in `scripts/` (notably `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py` and\\n`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`) are the natural home for extensions that\\nadd these checks.\\n\\n## See also\\n\\n- the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference — kernel-level blockers\\n  (`sorry`, `native_decide`, bare `axiom`, etc.);
