avoiding A5 (bypassing Mathlib) often starts with using\\n  Mathlib's names.\\n- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces [#449], [#451])\\n- [#449], [#451], [#477], [#493], [#494], [#495] — concrete trackers for\\n  the anti-patterns documented here.\\n\\n[#278]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/278\\n[#438]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/pull/438\\n[#307]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/307\\n[#449]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/449\\n[#451]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/451\\n[#477]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/477\\n[#491]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/pull/491\\n[#493]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/493\\n[#595]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/595\\n[#652]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/652\\n[#494]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/494\\n[#495]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/495\\n[#1379]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1379\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n35794:+{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_14\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc 'cat docs/project_conventions.md'\",\"aggregated_output\":\"# MIPStarRE-local convention addenda\\n\\nThe canonical convention documents live in the `lean-conventions` skill of\\n[texra-ai/texra-lean-skills](https://github.com/texra-ai/texra-lean-skills)\\n(auto-installed for Claude Code sessions via `.claude/settings.json`; other\\nagents: clone the repository and symlink the skill directories, per its\\nREADME). This file holds only\\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\\nrules never move here.\\n\\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\\n\\n### Linter warnings\\n\\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\\n\\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\\n\\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\\n\\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\\n\\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\\n\\n### Source-faithfulness checks\\n\\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\\n\\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\\nmathematically load-bearing.\\n\\nReviewers should also inspect `\\\\lean{}` and `\\\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\\n\\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\\n\\n### Companion document\\n\\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\\n\\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\\n\\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\\n`AGENTS.md`):\\n\\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\\n> conditional helper\\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\\n\\n### Axiom policy\\n\\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\\nthe axiomatic base.\\n\\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\\nfaithful to the paper.\\n\\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\n\\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\\n\\nSigns to watch for:\\n\\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\\n  semantics (e.g., a \\\"projective measurement\\\" definition that does not enforce\\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\\n- Definitions that \\\"work\\\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\\n  incompatible universes)\\n\\nWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\\nthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\\nprogress rather than enabling it.\\n\\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\\n\\nA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\\nif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\\nChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\\n\\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\\ntheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\\nrepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\\n`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\\ngeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\\nassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\\n\\nConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\\nbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\\nnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\\nhelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\\nobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\\nthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\\n`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\\nblueprint theorem with `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\nExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\\nfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\\nstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\\nbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\\nto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\\ntracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\\n\\nNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\\nto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\\ninstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\\nfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\\nconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\\nmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\\nstep of the source proof.\\n\\nFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\\n\\n- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\\n- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n\\n### Source-statement proof gaps\\n\\n**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\\n[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\\nproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\\nstructure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why\\nconditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a\\ntracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n35797:+{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_16\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc 'cat docs/formalization-patterns.md'\",\"aggregated_output\":\"# Formalization Patterns\\n\\nKey design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the\\ngap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.\\n\\nThis document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the\\nLean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize\\nthese patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits\\nin `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:\\n`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the\\nproof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.\\n\\n## Table of Contents\\n\\n1. [Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations](#pattern-1-source-faithful-statements-and-internal-proof-obligations)\\n2. [Blueprint–Lean synchronization](#pattern-2-blueprintlean-synchronization)\\n3. [Split-module architecture](#pattern-3-split-module-architecture)\\n4. [Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)\\n5. [Temporary obligation-structure pattern](#pattern-5-temporary-obligation-structure-pattern)\\n6. [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations\\n\\n### The rule\\n\\nA declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,\\nproposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal\\nencoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are\\nboth part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,\\nobligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present\\nin the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.\\n\\nThe project therefore distinguishes three objects.\\n\\n| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |\\n|--------|------------------|------------------|\\n| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\\\\lean{}`; statement-level `\\\\leanok` only when the statement matches |\\n| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |\\n| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\\\\leanok` |\\n\\nIt is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented\\nas the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly\\npoint, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,\\nor remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the\\nconditional helper is given a different name.\\n\\nThe preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or\\ndefinition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked\\n`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement\\nof a source-labelled theorem.\\n\\n### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily\\n\\n| Temporary reason | Explanation |\\n|------------------|-------------|\\n| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |\\n| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |\\n| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |\\n\\nThese reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain\\nwhy a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses\\nare being actively removed.\\n\\n### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input\\n\\n1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in\\n   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.\\n2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses\\n   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or\\n   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to\\n   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,\\n   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic\\n   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited\\n   statement says so.\\n3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical\\n   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A\\n   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as\\n   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.\\n4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name\\n   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization\\n   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof\\n   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked\\n   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint\\n   `\\\\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra\\n   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked\\n   `sorry` instead.\\n5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem\\n   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and\\n   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only\\n   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.\\n\\nIf a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional\\nhelper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper\\nhypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration\\nshould carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper\\ndependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the\\ninternal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation\\nwith a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the\\nmissing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem\\nstatement.\\n\\n### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations\\n\\nA new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,\\n`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,\\n`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in\\nthe def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the\\nreviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper\\nstatement or a Lean-only proof obligation.\\n\\nUse one of the following markers.\\n\\n| Marker | Use |\\n|--------|-----|\\n| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |\\n| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |\\n| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |\\n| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |\\n| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |\\n\\nProof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note\\nor tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.\\nIf such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis\\nto a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement\\nand leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.\\n\\n### Conditional helper boundary\\n\\n1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a\\n   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first\\n   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof\\n   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,\\n   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.\\n\\n2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**\\n   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper\\n   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled\\n   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport\\n   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct\\n   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing\\n   proof is an explicit `sorry`.\\n\\n   The former induction-section helper\\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it\\n   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor\\n   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem\\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the\\n   correct place for the missing work.\\n\\n3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of\\n   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a\\n   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal\\n   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a\\n   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or\\n   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.\\n\\n4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in\\n   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the\\n   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has\\n   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain\\n   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by\\n   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not\\n   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.\\n\\n   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper\\n   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the\\n   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient\\n   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be\\n   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.\\n\\n### Existing bridge-like declarations\\n\\nSeveral older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are\\ntransitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.\\nWhen such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and\\nkept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.\\n\\n| Declaration | Status to maintain |\\n|-------------|--------------------|\\n| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |\\n| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |\\n\\nThe former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.\\nThe former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,\\n`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and\\n`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.\\nUseful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing\\northonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the\\nsource-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.\\n\\nThe former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation\\nhas likewise been retired.  The spectral-truncation step is represented by the\\nsource-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction\\ntheorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,\\nrather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.\\n\\n### Retiring auxiliary declarations\\n\\nAn auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or\\nrenamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following\\nconditions hold.\\n\\n1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited\\n   outside result.\\n2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.\\n3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair\\n   data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper proof requires.\\n\\nIf such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, keep it\\nas a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.  It should\\nnot remain a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should not be\\nthe target of a source-labelled blueprint `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\n### Former proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean`\\n\\nThe former direct tracked proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean` and the\\nSection 6 successor route have been discharged under the corrected source\\nstatements.  The theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is the corrected\\ntwo-space source theorem.  The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has\\nbeen retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,\\npackage, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public\\nstatement.\\n\\n### Distinction from anti-patterns\\n\\nThis rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling\\n(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for\\npaper-labelled declarations:\\n\\n- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.\\n- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional\\n  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.\\n- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on\\n  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding\\n  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.\\n\\nObligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof\\ndebt under this pattern.  They should not be introduced merely because a proof\\nis blocked.  The preferred repair is to keep the paper-labelled statement\\nsource-faithful and make the exact missing mathematical step visible as a named\\nlemma or as a `sorry` in the theorem with the paper statement.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization\\n\\n### The three tags\\n\\nThe blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands\\nto link to Lean:\\n\\n| Tag | Meaning | Example |\\n|-----|---------|---------|\\n| `\\\\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\\\\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |\\n| `\\\\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\\\\leanok` |\\n| `\\\\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\\\\lean{...}` plus `\\\\leanok` inside `\\\\begin{proof}` |\\n| `\\\\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\\\\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |\\n\\nDo not use statement-level `\\\\leanok` for a source-labelled theorem whose Lean\\ndeclaration is conditional on bridge, residual, repair, proof-obligation input,\\ngeneric hypotheses bundle, or generic assumptions bundle\\ndata not present in the source.\\n\\n### Why some nodes show white in the dep graph\\n\\nThe dependency graph at\\n`https://LionSR.github.io/MIPStarRE/blueprint/dep_graph_document.html`\\ncolor-codes theorem nodes:\\n\\n- **Green**: proof-level `\\\\leanok` is present (the proof block is fully formalized)\\n- **White** (or white-border): `\\\\lean{}` exists but proof-level `\\\\leanok` is absent; may carry a statement-level `\\\\leanok` during staged development\\n- **Gray**: No `\\\\lean{}` tag\\n\\nAs of the session 49 audit (2026-05-07), the web dependency graph was\\nbuilt from an **older** `web.paux` file.  Almost all the nodes that\\nappeared non-green there (Ch09 pasting lemmas, Ch10 induction helpers)\\nalready have `\\\\leanok` in the current blueprint source files.  The web\\nbuild needs regeneration.\\n\\n### Current `\\\\leanok` status\\n\\nThe former deliberate withholding cases for `thm:orthonormalization`,\\n`thm:naimark`, `thm:main-induction`, and `thm:main-formal` have been resolved\\nin the current blueprint under the documented statement corrections.  The\\nproject now treats the factor-\\\\(400\\\\) large-\\\\(k\\\\) condition and the nonzero\\nsampling boundary \\\\(0<k\\\\) as corrections to the printed source statement, not\\nas proof obligations.  Under those corrected statements, the relevant blueprint\\nnodes carry proof-level `\\\\leanok` and the linked declarations are checked by the\\nstandard axiom and proof-debt audits.\\n\\n- **`thm:ld-pasting`** (ch09) and\\n  **`thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section`** (ch10): The paper theorem in\\n  `references/ldt-paper/ld-pasting.tex`, lines 12--50, assumes\\n  `k >= 400md` but does not state the nontrivial-regime inequalities as\\n  hypotheses.  The source-facing declaration `Pasting.ldPasting` keeps this\\n  unrestricted statement visible, including the direct degree-zero branch\\n  formerly tracked by issue #1622.  The restricted declaration\\n  `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` belongs in Lean-only remarks because it assumes\\n  `gamma <= 1`, `zeta <= 1`, `d <= q`, `0 < d`, and `1 <= k`.\\n\\n### The `\\\\uses{}` convention\\n\\n`\\\\uses{}` should appear:\\n\\n- On **statement blocks** (theorem/lemma/definition environments): only\\n  to record *mathematical* dependencies — other definitions or theorems\\n  whose statements are used in *stating* the current result (not in\\n  proving it).\\n- On **proof blocks** (`\\\\begin{proof}`): to record which lemmas are\\n  invoked in the proof.  This is the natural home for lemma-citation\\n  chains.\\n\\nA common mistake is placing proof-only `\\\\uses{}` on statement blocks.\\nFor the checklist item in the review:\\n`docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` covers this in the section on\\n`\\\\uses{}` placement.\\n\\n### Blueprint rebuild workflow\\n\\n```bash\\ncd blueprint\\nleanblueprint web   # generates the HTML with dep graph\\n```\\n\\nThe CI linting step effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from the\\n`blueprint/` directory.  After adding or removing `\\\\leanok` tags,\\nalways run this locally to verify the graph updates.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 3: Split-module architecture\\n\\n### Directory structure\\n\\nThe Lean codebase is organized into per-chapter subdirectories under\\n`MIPStarRE/LDT/`, each with its own internal structure:\\n\\n```\\nMIPStarRE/LDT/\\n├── Basic/                    # Parameters, operators, submeasurements, distributions\\n├── Test/                     # Test definitions, main theorem, error cascade\\n├── Preliminaries/            # Polynomials, finite fields, Cauchy–Schwarz, Fourier\\n├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/   # Orthonormalization, projective completion\\n├── MainInductionStep/        # Section 6 induction theorem\\n├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/  # Section 7–8 expansion, global variance\\n├── GlobalVariance/           # Section 8.5 (and related global variance machinery)\\n├── SelfImprovement/          # Section 9 self-improvement\\n├── CommutativityPoints/      # Section 10 commutativity setup\\n├── Tactic/                   # Section 10 proof orchestration utilities\\n├── Commutativity/            # Section 11 commutativity bounds\\n└── Pasting/                  # Section 12 pasting\\n```\\n\\n### Subdirectory layout convention\\n\\nEach subdirectory follows a consistent internal layout:\\n\\n```\\nSubModule/\\n├── Defs.lean        # New structures, type abbreviations, error-term definitions\\n├── Statements.lean   # Statement-level types (hypothesis bundles, conclusion shapes)\\n├── Theorems.lean     # Public re-export, when the section has one\\n└── Theorems/\\n    ├── Core.lean     # Main proof of the chapter's theorem\\n    ├── ...           # Supporting proof leaves\\n    └── Results.lean  # Re-export file for the proof leaves\\n```\\n\\nSome larger chapters (like `Pasting/` and `SelfImprovement/`) have more\\ninternal subdivisions (e.g., `Pasting/Bernoulli/`, `Pasting/Sandwich/`,\\n`SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/`).  When an outer `Theorems.lean` module is\\npresent, it imports the public proof leaves.\\n\\n### Why split instead of monolithic files?\\n\\n| Reason | Details |\\n|--------|---------|\\n| **Compilation parallelism** | Lean's per-file compilation is single-threaded per file; smaller files mean faster individual type-checking loops |\\n| **Dependency isolation** | A proof leaf in `Pasting/Sandwich/` only depends on `Pasting/Defs.lean` and `Pasting/Statements.lean`, not on the entire pasting proof chain |\\n| **Edit locality** | Changing a helper in `SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/AddInUStep12/Raw.lean` does not re-elaborate unrelated downstream leaves unless the helper's type changed |\\n| **Reviewability** | A 200-line proof leaf is easier to review than a 4000-line monolithic proof block |\\n| **Parallel agent work** | Different agents can work on different proof leaves concurrently without merge conflicts |\\n\\n### When *not* to split further\\n\\nDon't split a file just to have one theorem per file.  A single file\\ncontaining 3–5 related lemmas that share helper definitions and proof\\nstructure is better than 5 files each with one lemma and duplicate\\nhelper material.\\n\\nWhen splitting does happen, the new leaves, declarations, and module\\nnames must follow the mathematical naming norm in\\n`docs/mathematical_language.md`: name the mathematical boundary, not\\nthe paper line number, workflow step, or implementation phase.\\n\\n### Re-export files\\n\\nSee [Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)\\nbelow.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern\\n\\nPublic subdirectories with several proof leaves may have a root-level\\nre-export file that imports the source-facing leaves.  For example, the\\ntop-level LDT module imports the public section APIs:\\n\\n```lean\\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.ProjectivizationChain.Output\\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.MainInductionStep.Theorems.MainTheorems.Successor\\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.Pasting.Bernoulli.Final\\n```\\n\\nThe re-export module itself contains no new mathematical declarations. It is a\\npublic import convenience.  When no such public module exists, downstream code\\nshould import the specific leaf module whose declarations it uses.\\n\\nThe top-level re-export file is `MIPStarRE.lean`, which imports all\\nsubdirectories.  `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean` imports all LDT subdirectories.\\n\\n**When to add to a re-export file**: When a new proof leaf is added to a\\npublic theorem or definition subdirectory and the leaf is part of the intended\\nsection-level API, add its import to the relevant public module.\\n\\n**When not to add**: If a leaf is only used by one other leaf (internal\\nhelper), do not add it to a public re-export module; let the consumer import it\\ndirectly so its API surface does not leak.\\n\\n**When not to create another wrapper**: Do not add an intermediate module whose\\nonly purpose is to import a single leaf, or a wrapper that is itself imported\\nonly by a public re-export module.  The public module should import the\\nconcrete leaf directly.  Such one-step wrappers make the import graph harder to\\nread without recording any new mathematical boundary.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 5: Temporary obligation-structure pattern\\n\\nAn obligation structure is a `structure` whose fields are **proof obligations** that\\nhave not yet been discharged locally.  It is temporary proof debt.  Do not add a\\nnew obligation structure unless a direct source-faithful proof route has first been\\nattempted and the remaining obstruction is documented.\\n\\n### Removed anti-example\\n\\nThe old Section 9 interface bundled helper strong self-consistency,\\northonormalization, and final-field transport into a structure named\\n`SelfImprovementObligations`, then used a conditional theorem to obtain the\\nfull self-improvement conclusion.  That made the formalization look more\\ncomplete than it was.  The current code removes that bundle and leaves the\\nproof gap in `MIPStarRE.LDT.SelfImprovement.selfImprovement`.\\n\\n### Rules\\n\\n1. **Every obligation field must have a theorem that produces it somewhere**, or a\\n   live tracking issue (#1507, #422, etc.) explaining when it will be produced.\\n2. **Docstrings must name the tracking issue and paper source.**\\n3. **Fields must be the *assumptions* of the paper's proof, not the\\n   *conclusion* of the theorem** (see A1 anti-pattern in\\n   `docs/anti_patterns.md`).\\n4. **An obligation structure must not enter a source-labelled theorem statement.**\\n5. **When all fields are produced**, the obligation structure should be replaced by a\\n   theorem that calls the same proof without non-paper obligations.\\n\\n### Related patterns\\n\\n- `docs/anti_patterns.md` — A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis), A4\\n  (trivial default witnesses), A6 (external `*Statement` smuggles)\\n- Issue [#449] — hypothesis-smuggle ledger\\n- Issue [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis catalogue\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Pattern 6: Paper-gap documentation pattern\\n\\nWhen the Lean formalization intentionally diverges from the paper\\nstatement (corrected constant, different proof route, Mathlib-provided\\nlemma that replaces a paper step), document the divergence in\\n`docs/paper-gaps/` as a LaTeX note.\\n\\nThese notes follow a standard structure defined in\\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`:\\n\\n1. **At a glance**: difficulty, Mathlib surface, key APIs\\n2. **Key theorem forms**: what the paper states vs what Lean proves\\n3. **Proof analysis**: where the gap occurs and how Lean fills it\\n4. **Verdict**: whether the divergence is fatal, cosmetic, or tracked\\n\\nEach note is independent LaTeX and should be readable by a or by a\\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\\n\\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself. It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\\nblueprint theorem with `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\nExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt. It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,\\nmissing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical\\ndiscrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.\\nIn this repository such notes live under \\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/}. It should not merely say that \\\\Lean{} did\\nnot accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library\\nlemma was applied.\\n\\nThe documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A\\npolicy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist\\nnotes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical\\nprose.\\n\\n\\\\section{Concision and Readability}\\n\\nA paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue\\nin one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source\\nuses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit\\nchecked, and what the current verdict is. That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough\\nimplementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,\\nand the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.\\n\\nThe \\\\emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after\\n\\\\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the\\nreader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the\\nsource assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,\\nand the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long\\nderivation genuinely needs room.\\n\\nKeep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear\\nspecial case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed\\nequations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;\\navoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\\n   279\\tthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\\n   280\\t`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\\n   281\\tas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\\n   282\\tare visible at call sites.\\n   283\\t\\n   284\\t### Acceptable uses of this pattern\\n   285\\t\\n   286\\tNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\\n   287\\tthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\\n   288\\t`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\\n   289\\tany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \\\"the output satisfies\\n   290\\tP\\\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\\n   291\\tsmuggling a precondition.\\n   292\\t\\n   293\\t### How to fix it\\n   294\\t\\n   295\\tPick one of:\\n   296\\t\\n   297\\t1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\\n   298\\t   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\\n   299\\t   be passed.\\n   300\\t2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\\n   301\\t   the case, so theorems about \\\"the output\\\" now quantify only over the\\n   302\\t   `some` branch.\\n   303\\t3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\\n   304\\t   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\\n   305\\t   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\\n   306\\t\\n   307\\t### Classical-logic dependencies\\n   308\\t\\n   309\\tA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\\n   310\\tthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\\n   311\\tconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\\n   312\\timplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\\n   313\\tgate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\\n   314\\t#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\\n   315\\tThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\\n   316\\tnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\\n   317\\tbottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of\\n   318\\tclassical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.\\n   319\\t\\n   320\\t### Related issues\\n   321\\t\\n   322\\t- [#307] — placeholder Lagrange coefficient (original fallback tracker)\\n   323\\t- [#495] — the full pasting-interpolation catalogue\\n   324\\t\\n   325\\t---\\n   326\\t\\n   327\\t## A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials\\n   328\\t\\n   329\\t**Smell.** A theorem of the shape `∃ x, P x` is closed by picking\\n   330\\t`x := default`, `x := 0`, `x := 1`, or `x := Classical.arbitrary`, where the\\n   331\\tpaper names a *specific, non-trivial* `x` and derives `P x` from real\\n   332\\tstructure. The Lean claim is *mathematically* weaker because the Lean\\n   333\\ttheorem guarantees less than the paper's (it proves some-trivial-thing, not\\n   334\\tthe-specific-paper-thing). See [#449] for the full ledger.\\n   335\\t\\n   336\\t### Why it's bad\\n   337\\t\\n   338\\tThe theorem name matches a paper lemma but the witness has been cheapened\\n   339\\tinto a placeholder. Downstream theorems that inspect the witness get `0` or\\n   340\\t`default`, which is almost always useless. Consumers that \\\"use\\\" the lemma\\n   341\\tare really using the trivial `∃` and cannot proceed past the first attempt\\n   342\\tto pin the witness down.\\n   343\\t\\n   344\\t### How to spot it\\n   345\\t\\n   346\\t- `refine ⟨default, ?_⟩` / `exact ⟨default, ...⟩` / `refine ⟨0, ?_⟩` /\\n   347\\t  `exact ⟨1, ...⟩` inside a proof of a paper-cited existential.\\n   348\\t- `letI : Inhabited X := ⟨Classical.arbitrary X⟩` followed by a `let x :=\\n   349\\t  default`.\\n   350\\t- `Classical.arbitrary` / `Classical.choice` / `Nonempty.some` in proof\\n   351\\t  bodies (as opposed to typeclass definitions).\\n   352\\t- Identifier suffix `...Witness := default` on a bundled output.\\n   353\\t\\n   354\\t### Concrete example\\n   355\\t\\n   356\\tFrom the ledger in [#449]:\\n   357\\t\\n   358\\t- `lem:sdp` / `sdp` — primal witness is `T := default` (a zero\\n   359\\t  submeasurement) and dual witness `Z := 1`. The paper requires a specific\\n   360\\t  feasible pair; the Lean version proves only that some arbitrary pair exists,\\n   361\\t  which always does.\\n   362\\t- `lem:projective-low-rank-sum` / `projectiveLowRankSum` — auxiliary\\n   363\\t  projective measurement `t := (default : ProjMeas Outcome ι)`. The paper\\n   364\\t  constructs `(auxSpace, T_a)` from the eigenvector basis of each rounded\\n   365\\t  `R_a`; the Lean version picks a zero-dimensional placeholder, which is\\n   366\\t  disconnected from the paper's SVD derivation.\\n   367\\t- ~~`lem:global-rewrite` / `globalRewrite` — decomposition witness is\\n   368\\t  `default`~~ (historical; resolved by PRs #527 and #542). The live theorem now\\n   369\\t  uses `canonicalGlobalVarianceDecomposition`, and\\n   370\\t  `globalVarianceTraceWitness` consumes the centered residual family\\n   371\\t  `u ↦ A^u - A_{\\\\mathrm{avg}}` rather than ignoring the witness.\\n   372\\t\\n   373\\t### Acceptable uses\\n   374\\t\\n   375\\tNon-computable instances required for typeclass plumbing, such as\\n   376\\t`Nonempty (Polynomial params)` inhabited by the zero polynomial, are fine when\\n   377\\tthey are used only to *inhabit* a type, not to discharge a paper-cited\\n   378\\texistential.  Degenerate measurements should be constructed explicitly with a\\n   379\\tspecified outcome rather than supplied by an ambient `Inhabited` instance.  The\\n   380\\tsmell is specifically about `default` showing up in the proof of a *theorem\\n   381\\tnamed after a paper result*.\\n   382\\t\\n   383\\t### How to fix it\\n   384\\t\\n   385\\t- Construct the paper's witness explicitly. If the ingredients are not yet\\n   386\\t  formalized (e.g., Mathlib SVD, spectral decomposition), extract a bridge\\n   387\\t  lemma that *constructs* the witness from the missing Mathlib facts, and\\n   388\\t  track the Mathlib gap as a separate issue.\\n   389\\t- Keep the existential statement, but strengthen the conclusion so that\\n   390\\t  `x := default` no longer satisfies it (e.g., \\\"there exists `x` *with*\\n   391\\t  rank `m`\\\", not merely \\\"there exists `x`\\\").\\n   392\\t- If the witness cannot yet be constructed, keep the source-facing existential\\n   393\\t  statement and expose the missing construction as a named proof obligation.\\n   394\\t  Replacing `default` by an explicit bridge hypothesis is still an A1-grade\\n   395\\t  placeholder, not a proof of the paper theorem.\\n   396\\t\\n   397\\t### Related issues\\n   398\\t\\n   399\\t- [#449] — master ledger; all three known cases are already listed\\n   400\\t\\n   401\\t---\\n   402\\t\\n   403\\t## A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib\\n   404\\t\\n   405\\t**Smell.** Lean code re-declares or re-proves something that already lives\\n   406\\tin Mathlib, or builds a tower of custom lemmas that never bottom out in\\n   407\\tMathlib / Lean core. The proof \\\"works\\\" only because the internal custom\\n   408\\tstatements are compatible with each other — it is a closed ecosystem that\\n   409\\tdoesn't ground in the reference library.\\n   410\\t\\n   411\\tThis is the \\\"scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\\" section of\\n   412\\t[`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md) in concrete examples. The two\\n   413\\tflavours:\\n   414\\t\\n   415\\t1. **Re-proving Mathlib.** Writing `private lemma my_add_comm : a + b = b + a`\\n   416\\t   when `add_comm` exists.\\n   417\\t2. **Custom types that shadow Mathlib.** Defining `MyMeasurement` instead of\\n   418\\t   using `MeasureTheory.Measure`, `MyMatrix` instead of `Matrix`,\\n   419\\t   `MyHermitian` instead of `Matrix.IsHermitian`. The custom version may be\\n   420\\t   definitionally equal to (or coercible from) the Mathlib version, but if\\n   421\\t   it isn't, every consumer must reprove everything.\\n   422\\t\\n   423\\t### Why it's bad\\n   424\\t\\n   425\\t1. The duplicated statements aren't audited by Mathlib's community, so they\\n   426\\t   may be subtly wrong (wrong edge case, wrong universe, wrong typeclass).\\n   427\\t2. When the real Mathlib proof is needed (for a key gap lemma), the custom\\n   428\\t   tower must be rewritten to interoperate — often via a painful coercion\\n   429\\t   layer that reintroduces every fact.\\n   430\\t3. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because \\\"our\\n   431\\t   version is simpler,\\\" the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.\\n   432\\t\\n   433\\t### How to spot it\\n   434\\t\\n   435\\t- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis\\n   436\\t  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).\\n   437\\t- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a\\n   438\\t  standard concept.\\n   439\\t- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib\\n   440\\t  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.\\n   441\\t- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`\\n   442\\t  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,\\n   443\\t  analysis, measure theory).\\n   444\\t\\n   445\\t### How to fix it\\n   446\\t\\n   447\\tBefore writing a new lemma, spend one minute on:\\n   448\\t\\n   449\\t- `exact?` / `apply?` on the goal.\\n   450\\t- `#find` / `Loogle` for the statement shape.\\n   451\\t- `rg -n \\\"theorem.*X\\\" .lake/packages/mathlib/` for a keyword.\\n   452\\t\\n   453\\tIf Mathlib has it, use it. If it doesn't, consider whether the missing\\n   454\\tlemma should be upstreamed (file an issue against Mathlib, or at least a\\n   455\\tTODO pointing at the gap). The project already has this mandate — see the\\n   456\\t\\\"Mathlib Integration\\\" section of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):\\n   457\\t\\n   458\\t> Scout Mathlib first (`exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source)\\n   459\\t\\n   460\\tA5 is what happens when that step is skipped.\\n   461\\t\\n   462\\t### Audit cross-reference\\n   463\\t\\n   464\\t`audits/` contains chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency scouting\\n   465\\treports. If a section of the code review says \\\"this could use Mathlib\\n   466\\tlemma X\\\", it belongs in a specific `audits/*.md` file for that chapter.\\n   467\\t\\n   468\\t---\\n   469\\t\\n   470\\t## A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles\\n   471\\t\\n   472\\t**Smell.** A theorem takes a hypothesis of type `SomeStatement` (or\\n   473\\t`SomeWitness`, `SomeOutput`, etc.) that is defined elsewhere and intended\\n   474\\tto represent an external mathematical result, but there is no theorem\\n   475\\tconstructing it from the hypotheses under which the paper uses it. The Lean\\n   476\\tstatement is then:\\n   477\\t\\\"assuming the external result, the Lean conclusion holds.\\\" That is\\n   478\\tsometimes legitimate (e.g., a cite to a book whose formalization we don't\\n   479\\tplan to do), and sometimes a cover for locally-unwanted work.\\n   480\\t\\n   481\\tThis overlaps with A1 but is subtler: the hypothesis isn't the\\n   482\\t*current theorem's* conclusion, it's an *independently-named* claim that\\n   483\\thappens to unblock the current proof.\\n   484\\t\\n   485\\t### Acceptable external smuggles\\n   486\\t\\n   487\\t- **Genuine external citations.** `PolishchukSpielmanClassicalSoundnessStatement`\\n   488\\t  cites the Polishchuk–Spielman theorem; we don't plan to formalize it.\\n   489\\t- **Mathlib gaps we can't fill.** `hMatrixChernoff` in `chernoffBernoulliMatrix`\\n   490\\t  is a Mathlib matrix-Chernoff-type statement; we flagged the gap upstream.\\n   491\\t- **Tracked internal obligations.** A `*Statement` that has an open sub-issue\\n   492\\t  and a named construction theorem target is trackable proof debt. It is still\\n   493\\t  not an acceptable extra hypothesis on a source-labelled paper theorem.\\n   494\\t\\n   495\\t### Unacceptable external smuggles\\n   496\\t\\n   497\\t- A `*Statement` with no open tracking issue, no docstring explaining the\\n   498\\t  mathematical gap, and no consumer-side comment flagging the smuggle.\\n   499\\t- A `*Statement` whose body is the theorem's conclusion, wearing a different\\n   500\\t  name (A1 in disguise).\\n   501\\t- A `*Statement` used to close a lemma whose paper version does not require\\n   502\\t  any such external assumption (silent strengthening of the Lean theorem\\n   503\\t  relative to the paper's).\\n   504\\t\\n   505\\t### How to spot it\\n   506\\t\\n   507\\tGrep for these suffixes: `*Statement`, `*Witness`, `*Claim`,\\n   508\\t`*Conclusion`, `*Output`, `*Input`, `*Hypothesis`, `*Requirement`,\\n   509\\t`*Assumption`, `*Package` (that isn't a `*BridgePackage`). For each, ask:\\n   510\\t\\n   511\\t- Is there a theorem anywhere that **constructs** a value of this type from the\\n   512\\t  paper hypotheses?\\n   513\\t- If not, is the absence explained in a docstring / tracking issue /\\n   514\\t  `audits/` entry?\\n   515\\t- Does the paper depend on an external theorem of this shape?\\n   516\\t\\n   517\\tIf any answer is \\\"no\\\", the structure is an unacceptable smuggle.\\n   518\\t\\n   519\\t### Current status (audited 2026-05-08)\\n   520\\t\\n   521\\tThe May 2026 re-audit\\n   522\\t([`audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md`](../blob/main/audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md))\\n   523\\tclassified 39 `*Statement` structures (102 declarations total across the\\n   524\\textended suffix sweep of `*Witness`/`*Conclusion`/`*Input`/etc.).\\n   525\\t\\n   526\\tThe live ledger is [#1379], replacing the now-closed [#449] (2026-05-01) and\\n   527\\t[#451] (2026-04-30). Headline counts from the re-audit: 33 grounded, 2 tracked\\n   528\\tsmuggle, 2 external citation, 1 paper-faithful packaging, 1 dead. Without a live\\n   529\\tledger, **5 `*Statement` structures landed between 2026-04-18 and 2026-05-08\\n   530\\twithout a tracker entry** — the gap this policy fixes.\\n   531\\t\\n   532\\tThe Section 5 spectral-truncation chain is now an example of the preferred\\n   533\\tmigration: the old `SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation has been removed, and\\n   534\\tlater arguments call direct constructors for `SpectralTruncationStatement`\\n   535\\tinstead of carrying an `Input` wrapper.\\n   536\\t\\n   537\\tIf you add a new `*Statement`-style structure to this codebase, include a\\n   538\\tdef-site docstring with its paper origin (per the \\\"earn your place\\\" policy in\\n   539\\t[#1379]). If no construction theorem exists yet, file a sub-issue in [#1379]\\n   540\\tand ship the source-faithful construction theorem with an explicit unfinished\\n   541\\tproof obligation. Do not add the structure as a new source-theorem hypothesis\\n   542\\tmerely to keep downstream declarations compiling.\\n   543\\t\\n   544\\t### Merge gate — new `*Statement` / `*Witness` / `*Input` structures\\n   545\\t\\n   546\\tTo prevent dead scaffolds from landing unnoticed (the 5-structure gap of\\n   547\\t2026-04-18–2026-05-08), every PR that introduces a new `structure XStatement`,\\n   548\\t`structure XWitness`, `structure XInput`, `abbrev XStatement`, or\\n   549\\t`abbrev XInput` must satisfy **at least one** of these before merge:\\n   550\\t\\n   551\\t1. **Has a construction theorem.** A theorem that constructs a value of this\\n   552\\t   type from the appropriate paper hypotheses appears in the same PR or an\\n   553\\t   already-merged ancestor. If the proof is not finished, the theorem must carry\\n   554\\t   the explicit tracked proof obligation rather than moving the assertion into a\\n   555\\t   paper-facing theorem's hypotheses.\\n   556\\t2. **Has a consumer.** A theorem that takes a value of this type as a\\n   557\\t   hypothesis appears in the same PR or an already-merged ancestor.\\n   558\\t3. **Has a ledger entry.** A classification comment (G / E / T / P / D, per\\n   559\\t   the verdict key in [#1379]) is posted on [#1379] as an issue comment, and\\n   560\\t   the structure's def-site docstring links to that comment.\\n   561\\t\\n   562\\tStructures that satisfy none of the above are dead on arrival and must not\\n   563\\tmerge.\\n   564\\t\\n   565\\t### Related issues\\n   566\\t\\n   567\\t- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces closed [#449] / [#451])\\n   568\\t- [#449] — historical paper-wide gap tracker (closed 2026-05-01)\\n   569\\t- [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis tracker (closed 2026-04-30)\\n   570\\t- [#278] — the original \\\"derive `PermInvState` internally\\\" discussion\\n   571\\t\\n   572\\t---\\n   573\\t\\n   574\\t## Reviewer checklist\\n   575\\t\\n   576\\tUse this alongside the blocker\\n   577\\tlist in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)\\n   578\\tchecklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper\\n   579\\tresult, ask:\\n   580\\t\\n   581\\t- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the\\n   582\\t      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.\\n   583\\t- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If\\n   584\\t      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match\\n   585\\t      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.\\n   586\\t- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if\\n   587\\t      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature\\n   588\\t      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.\\n   589\\t- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an\\n   590\\t      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness\\n   591\\t      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.\\n   592\\t- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a\\n   593\\t      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it\\n   594\\t      (A5).\\n   595\\t- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /\\n   596\\t      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its\\n   597\\t      grounding plan (A6)?\\n   598\\t- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's\\n   599\\t      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences\\n   600\\t      as ⚠️S in [#1379].\\n   601\\t\\n   602\\tA lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is\\n   603\\tscaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with\\n   604\\t`\\\\leanok` until the gap is closed).\\n   605\\t\\n   606\\t## CI prevention\\n   607\\t\\n   608\\tMechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:\\n   609\\t\\n   610\\t- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use\\n   611\\t  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current\\n   612\\t  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses\\n   613\\t  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares\\n   614\\t  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers\\n   615\\t  separately. When [#438] lands (`\\\\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same\\n   616\\t  idea to all `\\\\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any\\n   617\\t  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion\\n   618\\t  structure, warn.\\n   619\\t- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where\\n   620\\t  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\\\\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases\\n   621\\t  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in\\n   622\\t  an allow-list.\\n   623\\t- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,\\n   624\\t  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have\\n   625\\t  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.\\n   626\\t- **A4 (default witnesses).** Grep `:= default`, `refine ⟨default`, `exact\\n   627\\t  ⟨default`, `Classical.arbitrary` inside proof bodies (not typeclass\\n   628\\t  definitions).
