This file holds only\\n     8\\tMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\\n     9\\trules never move here.\\n    10\\t\\n    11\\t## Style (MATHLIB_style)\\n    12\\t\\n    13\\t### Linter warnings\\n    14\\t\\n    15\\tDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\\n    16\\tbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\\n    17\\tblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\\n    18\\tmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\\n    19\\t\\n    20\\tFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\\n    21\\t\\n    22\\t- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\\n    23\\t- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\\n    24\\t  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\\n    25\\t- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\\n    26\\t- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\\n    27\\t  silencing `linter.flexible`.\\n    28\\t\\n    29\\tIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\\n    30\\texception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\\n    31\\t`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\\n    32\\tSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\\n    33\\tthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\\n    34\\t\\n    35\\t## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\\n    36\\t\\n    37\\t### Source-faithfulness checks\\n    38\\t\\n    39\\tFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\\n    40\\tstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\\n    41\\tapplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\\n    42\\t`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\\n    43\\tsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\\n    44\\tcorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\\n    45\\t\\n    46\\tReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\\n    47\\trepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\\n    48\\tor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\\n    49\\tpositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\\n    50\\tencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\\n    51\\tmathematically load-bearing.\\n    52\\t\\n    53\\tReviewers should also inspect `\\\\lean{}` and `\\\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\\n    54\\tblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\\n    55\\ttheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\\n    56\\tAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\\n    57\\tremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\\n    58\\t\\n    59\\t## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\\n    60\\t\\n    61\\t### Companion document\\n    62\\t\\n    63\\t> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\\n    64\\t> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\\n    65\\t> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\\n    66\\t> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\\n    67\\t> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\\n    68\\t> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\\n    69\\t> Consult it alongside this file during review.\\n    70\\t\\n    71\\t### Project paper-realignment protocol\\n    72\\t\\n    73\\tThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\\n    74\\t`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\\n    75\\tfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\\n    76\\t`AGENTS.md`):\\n    77\\t\\n    78\\t> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\\n    79\\t> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\\n    80\\t> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\\n    81\\t> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\\n    82\\t> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\\n    83\\t> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\\n    84\\t> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\\n    85\\t> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\\n    86\\t> conditional helper\\n    87\\t> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\\n    88\\t> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\\n    89\\t> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\\n    90\\t\\n    91\\t### Axiom policy\\n    92\\t\\n    93\\tWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\\n    94\\tprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\\n    95\\tdeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\\n    96\\t`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\\n    97\\t`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\\n    98\\tthe axiomatic base.\\n    99\\t\\n   100\\tThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\\n   101\\ttheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\\n   102\\tcaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\\n   103\\tproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\\n   104\\tconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\\n   105\\tfaithful to the paper.\\n   106\\t\\n   107\\t### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\n   108\\t\\n   109\\tThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\\n   110\\ttheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\\n   111\\tmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\\n   112\\t\\n   113\\tSigns to watch for:\\n   114\\t\\n   115\\t- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\\n   116\\t  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\\n   117\\t  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\\n   118\\t- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\\n   119\\t  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\\n   120\\t- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\\n   121\\t  semantics (e.g., a \\\"projective measurement\\\" definition that does not enforce\\n   122\\t  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\\n   123\\t- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\\n   124\\t  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\\n   125\\t- Definitions that \\\"work\\\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\\n   126\\t  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\\n   127\\t  incompatible universes)\\n   128\\t\\n   129\\tWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\\n   130\\tthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\\n   131\\tscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\\n   132\\tprogress rather than enabling it.\\n   133\\t\\n   134\\t### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\\n   135\\t\\n   136\\tA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\\n   137\\tif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\\n   138\\tChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\\n   139\\tstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\\n   140\\tdocumented mathematical necessity.\\n   141\\t\\n   142\\tThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\\n   143\\textra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\\n   144\\ttheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\\n   145\\trepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\\n   146\\t`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\\n   147\\tgeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\\n   148\\tassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\\n   149\\t\\n   150\\tConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\\n   151\\tbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\\n   152\\tnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\\n   153\\thelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\\n   154\\tobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\\n   155\\tthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\\n   156\\t`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\\n   157\\tblueprint theorem with `\\\\leanok`.\\n   158\\t\\n   159\\tExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\\n   160\\tfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\\n   161\\tstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\\n   162\\tbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\\n   163\\tto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\\n   164\\ttracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\\n   165\\t\\n   166\\tNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\\n   167\\tto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\\n   168\\tinstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\\n   169\\tfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\\n   170\\tconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\\n   171\\tmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\\n   172\\tstep of the source proof.\\n   173\\t\\n   174\\tFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\\n   175\\t\\n   176\\t- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\\n   177\\t- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\\n   178\\t- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n   179\\t  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n   180\\t\\n   181\\t### Source-statement proof gaps\\n   182\\t\\n   183\\t**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\\n   184\\t[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\\n   185\\tproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\\n   186\\tstructure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why\\n   187\\tconditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a\\n   188\\ttracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n36014:+{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_30\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"nl -ba docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex | sed -n '1,360p'\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"     1\\t\\\\documentclass[11pt]{article}\\n     2\\t\\n     3\\t\\\\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}\\n     4\\t\\\\usepackage{xurl}\\n     5\\t\\\\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}\\n     6\\t\\\\setlength{\\\\emergencystretch}{2em}\\n     7\\t\\n     8\\t\\\\input{command}\\n     9\\t\\n    10\\t\\\\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}\\n    11\\t\\\\author{}\\n    12\\t\\\\date{2026-04-29}\\n    13\\t\\n    14\\t\\\\begin{document}\\n    15\\t\\\\maketitle\\n    16\\t\\n    17\\t\\\\section{Purpose}\\n    18\\t\\n    19\\tWhen a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source\\n    20\\tshould remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,\\n    21\\tmissing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical\\n    22\\tdiscrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.\\n    23\\tIn this repository such notes live under \\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same\\n    24\\tprinciple applies when the formal development has already diverged from the\\n    25\\tcited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by\\n    26\\tusing a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem\\n    27\\thas a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a\\n    28\\trecord of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or\\n    29\\tmathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.\\n    30\\t\\n    31\\tThe note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the\\n    32\\tcited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or\\n    33\\thypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.\\n    34\\tIf the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the\\n    35\\treplacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially\\n    36\\timportant when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from\\n    37\\tMathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should\\n    38\\tstate the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is\\n    39\\tspecialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and\\n    40\\tconclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \\\\Lean{} did\\n    41\\tnot accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library\\n    42\\tlemma was applied.\\n    43\\t\\n    44\\tThe documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A\\n    45\\tpolicy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist\\n    46\\tnotes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical\\n    47\\tprose.\\n    48\\t\\n    49\\t\\\\section{Concision and Readability}\\n    50\\t\\n    51\\tA paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue\\n    52\\tin one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source\\n    53\\tuses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit\\n    54\\tchecked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short\\n    55\\t\\\\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved\\n    56\\tformalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough\\n    57\\timplementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,\\n    58\\tand the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.\\n    59\\t\\n    60\\tThe \\\\emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after\\n    61\\t\\\\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the\\n    62\\treader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the\\n    63\\tsource assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,\\n    64\\tand the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long\\n    65\\tderivation genuinely needs room.\\n    66\\t\\n    67\\tKeep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear\\n    68\\tspecial case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed\\n    69\\tequations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;\\n    70\\tavoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The\\n    71\\tblueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem\\n    72\\tforms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data\\n    73\\tbelongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.\\n    74\\t\\n    75\\tIf the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and\\n    76\\tstop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.\\n    77\\tIf the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link\\n    78\\tthe issue or pull request in a footnote.\\n    79\\t\\n    80\\t\\\\section{When the Investigation Starts}\\n    81\\t\\n    82\\tThe investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather\\n    83\\tthan merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough\\n    84\\tthat, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal\\n    85\\tstatement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional\\n    86\\thypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which\\n    87\\tthe prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited\\n    88\\targument.\\n    89\\t\\n    90\\tThe same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered\\n    91\\tafter the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has\\n    92\\talready changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,\\n    93\\tinserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different\\n    94\\tformal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all\\n    95\\trelevant files already compile.\\n    96\\t\\n    97\\tAt this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still\\n    98\\tlocal.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an\\n    99\\tintermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a\\n   100\\tmissing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus\\n   101\\tthe trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a\\n   102\\treal mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be\\n   103\\tformalized.\\n   104\\t\\n   105\\tA failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is\\n   106\\tnot enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary\\n   107\\tmathematics.\\n   108\\t\\n   109\\tSometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:\\n   110\\tthe formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an\\n   111\\texisting library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.\\n   112\\tThese are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When\\n   113\\tsuch an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that\\n   114\\tdescribes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap\\n   115\\tnote, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the\\n   116\\tmathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the\\n   117\\timplementation.\\n   118\\t\\n   119\\t\\\\section{When to Write a Note}\\n   120\\t\\n   121\\tA note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer\\n   122\\tmatch as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical\\n   123\\testimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed\\n   124\\tconclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are\\n   125\\tidentified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,\\n   126\\tprobabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of\\n   127\\ta map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction\\n   128\\tbetween a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation\\n   129\\trelation.\\n   130\\t\\n   131\\tA note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a\\n   132\\tsource-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as\\n   133\\tbridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a\\n   134\\tdeclaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,\\n   135\\tand should not be introduced merely to avoid a \\\\verb|sorry|.  The note must say\\n   136\\tplainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem\\n   137\\tform that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or\\n   138\\tremoval plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with\\n   139\\t\\\\verb|\\\\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.\\n   140\\t\\n   141\\tChanging a Lean theorem away from the statement in\\n   142\\t\\\\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should\\n   143\\tnot make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical\\n   144\\tnecessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.\\n   145\\t\\n   146\\tWhen an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any\\n   147\\targument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining\\n   148\\tbridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal\\n   149\\tdevelopment should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing\\n   150\\tproof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as\\n   151\\tthough it were the paper theorem.\\n   152\\t\\n   153\\tThis requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as\\n   154\\ta discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,\\n   155\\tand denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain\\n   156\\tin which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such\\n   157\\tboundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper\\n   158\\targument.\\n   159\\t\\n   160\\tA note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an\\n   161\\tintermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or\\n   162\\tinserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited\\n   163\\targument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the\\n   164\\tfinal theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library\\n   165\\ttheorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the\\n   166\\tcited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It\\n   167\\tshould explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result\\n   168\\tsays, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,\\n   169\\tand why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the\\n   170\\tcited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note\\n   171\\tshould say what has been checked and what remains unknown.\\n   172\\t\\n   173\\t\\\\section{Counterexamples}\\n   174\\t\\n   175\\tIf the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying\\n   176\\tthat the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the\\n   177\\tsmallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example\\n   178\\tshould be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:\\n   179\\tthe hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.\\n   180\\t\\n   181\\tWhen feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \\\\Lean{}.  This is\\n   182\\tespecially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or\\n   183\\totherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the\\n   184\\twhole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content\\n   185\\tof the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in\\n   186\\ta footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should\\n   187\\tstill explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.\\n   188\\t\\n   189\\t\\\\section{Revision of a Note}\\n   190\\t\\n   191\\tA paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical\\n   192\\tobstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be\\n   193\\trevised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \\\\Lean{}\\n   194\\tdeclarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final\\n   195\\tclassification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and\\n   196\\twhich point remains unsettled.\\n   197\\t\\n   198\\tLater revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should\\n   199\\trewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present\\n   200\\tmathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state\\n   201\\tthe current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier\\n   202\\tdiscussion.\\n   203\\t\\n   204\\t\\\\section{Form of the Note}\\n   205\\t\\n   206\\tEach note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant\\n   207\\tsource article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the\\n   208\\toriginal passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may\\n   209\\tbe linked with \\\\verb|\\\\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be\\n   210\\trecorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should\\n   211\\tserve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized\\n   212\\taround the mathematical assertion and its proof.\\n   213\\t\\n   214\\tThe note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for\\n   215\\tmeasurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters\\n   216\\tshould be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the\\n   217\\tstate should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can\\n   218\\tbe done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the\\n   219\\tassertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as\\n   220\\t\\\\verb|\\\\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.\\n   221\\t\\n   222\\tOnly the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar\\n   223\\tsubstitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote\\n   224\\ta long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or\\n   225\\tproposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or\\n   226\\tlogical implication in which the discrepancy appears.\\n   227\\t\\n   228\\tDisplayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the\\n   229\\tsource estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and\\n   230\\tthe calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a\\n   231\\tdisplayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on\\n   232\\tthe right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical\\n   233\\tassertion itself.  The standard \\\\texttt{amsmath} command \\\\verb|\\\\tag| is the\\n   234\\tright mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only\\n   235\\tif the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned\\n   236\\tdisplay, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than\\n   237\\tforcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short\\n   238\\tscalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the\\n   239\\tsentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed\\n   240\\tformula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.\\n   241\\t\\n   242\\tBibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in\\n   243\\t\\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from\\n   244\\t\\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,\\n   245\\tthe local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed\\n   246\\tequations.\\n   247\\t\\n   248\\tBlueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with\\n   249\\t\\\\verb|\\\\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in\\n   250\\t\\\\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,\\n   251\\twhether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings\\n   252\\tand comments use the repository path form \\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.\\n   253\\t\\n   254\\tThe note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if\\n   255\\tthere is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written\\n   256\\tin ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should\\n   257\\tbe supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in\\n   258\\tfootnotes.\\n   259\\t\\n   260\\tThe conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,\\n   261\\tthat the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a\\n   262\\tharmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level\\n   263\\tgap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the\\n   264\\tmathematics, not the amount of formal work required.\\n   265\\t\\n   266\\t\\\\section{Decision Principle}\\n   267\\t\\n   268\\tThe formal development should not silently replace the cited assertion by a\\n   269\\tdifferent one.  If the formal statement differs from the cited source, the\\n   270\\treason for the difference should be written down.  Conversely, the note should\\n   271\\tnot overstate the conclusion.  A wrong intermediate scalar is not a fatal gap in\\n   272\\tthe theorem if the corrected scalar is bounded by the error parameter appearing\\n   273\\tin the theorem statement.\\n   274\\t\\n   275\\t\\\\end{document}\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n36018:+{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_32\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"nl -ba docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md | sed -n '1,280p'\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"     1\\t# Lean Proof Integrity Rules\\n     2\\t\\n     3\\tThis file is the **single source of truth** for proof integrity checks in this\\n     4\\trepository. All CI workflows and review prompts should reference this file\\n     5\\trather than duplicating the rules inline.\\n     6\\t\\n     7\\t> **Lean version**: 4.x (Lean 3 keywords like `constant` do not apply)\\n     8\\t\\n     9\\t> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\\n    10\\t> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check below yet still\\n    11\\t> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\\n    12\\t> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\\n    13\\t> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\\n    14\\t> Consult it alongside this file during review.\\n    15\\t\\n    16\\t> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\\n    17\\t> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\\n    18\\t> blocker below may be temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\\n    19\\t> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\\n    20\\t> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\\n    21\\t> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\\n    22\\t> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\\n    23\\t> conditional helper\\n    24\\t> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\\n    25\\t> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\\n    26\\t> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\\n    27\\t\\n    28\\t---\\n    29\\t\\n    30\\t## Blockers\\n    31\\t\\n    32\\tThese patterns **must** be resolved before merging.\\n    33\\t\\n    34\\t### Direct proof holes\\n    35\\t\\n    36\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n    37\\t|---------|------|\\n    38\\t| `sorry` | Axiomatically closes any goal — the proof is incomplete |\\n    39\\t| `admit` | Tactic alias for `sorry` |\\n    40\\t\\n    41\\t### Kernel / type system bypasses\\n    42\\t\\n    43\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n    44\\t|---------|------|\\n    45\\t| `native_decide` | Relies on trusted native evaluation / compiler; banned in Mathlib for soundness and process reasons |\\n    46\\t| `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce` | Type system bypass — can fabricate any proof term |\\n    47\\t| `lcProof` | Low-level proof fabrication primitive — can prove `False` |\\n    48\\t| `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat` | Kernel reduction primitives exploitable for unsound proofs |\\n    49\\t\\n    50\\t### Axiom smuggling\\n    51\\t\\n    52\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n    53\\t|---------|------|\\n    54\\t| `axiom` declarations | Introduces unproven assumptions that could be inconsistent; must be explicitly justified |\\n    55\\t\\n    56\\tWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\\n    57\\tprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\\n    58\\tdeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\\n    59\\t`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\\n    60\\t`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\\n    61\\tthe axiomatic base.\\n    62\\t\\n    63\\tThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\\n    64\\ttheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\\n    65\\tcaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\\n    66\\tproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\\n    67\\tconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\\n    68\\tfaithful to the paper.\\n    69\\t\\n    70\\t### Circular reasoning\\n    71\\t\\n    72\\tLean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical\\n    73\\tcircularity**:\\n    74\\t\\n    75\\t- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a\\n    76\\t  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis\\n    77\\t- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are\\n    78\\t  only used to prove that goal\\n    79\\t- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve\\n    80\\t  the goal without any real argument\\n    81\\t- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable\\n    82\\t  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems\\n    83\\t- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine\\n    84\\t  derivation\\n    85\\t- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the\\n    86\\t  goal\\n    87\\t\\n    88\\t### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)\\n    89\\t\\n    90\\tProofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:\\n    91\\t\\n    92\\t- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving\\n    93\\t  `add_comm` instead of importing it)\\n    94\\t- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in\\n    95\\t  Mathlib\\n    96\\t- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core\\n    97\\t- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix\\n    98\\t  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\n    99\\t- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma\\n   100\\t\\n   101\\tWhen flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,\\n   102\\t`library_search`). If an equivalent exists, cite the Mathlib lemma and module\\n   103\\tpath. If not, state \\\"no equivalent found\\\" with search evidence.\\n   104\\t\\n   105\\t### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\\n   106\\t\\n   107\\tThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\\n   108\\ttheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\\n   109\\tmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\\n   110\\t\\n   111\\tSigns to watch for:\\n   112\\t\\n   113\\t- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\\n   114\\t  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\\n   115\\t  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\\n   116\\t- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\\n   117\\t  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\\n   118\\t- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\\n   119\\t  semantics (e.g., a \\\"projective measurement\\\" definition that does not enforce\\n   120\\t  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\\n   121\\t- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\\n   122\\t  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\\n   123\\t- Definitions that \\\"work\\\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\\n   124\\t  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\\n   125\\t  incompatible universes)\\n   126\\t\\n   127\\tWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\\n   128\\tthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\\n   129\\tscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\\n   130\\tprogress rather than enabling it.\\n   131\\t\\n   132\\t### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\\n   133\\t\\n   134\\tA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\\n   135\\tif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\\n   136\\tChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\\n   137\\tstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\\n   138\\tdocumented mathematical necessity.\\n   139\\t\\n   140\\tThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\\n   141\\textra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\\n   142\\ttheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\\n   143\\trepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\\n   144\\t`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\\n   145\\tgeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\\n   146\\tassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\\n   147\\t\\n   148\\tConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\\n   149\\tbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\\n   150\\tnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\\n   151\\thelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\\n   152\\tobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\\n   153\\tthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\\n   154\\t`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\\n   155\\tblueprint theorem with `\\\\leanok`.\\n   156\\t\\n   157\\tExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\\n   158\\tfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\\n   159\\tstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\\n   160\\tbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\\n   161\\tto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\\n   162\\ttracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\\n   163\\t\\n   164\\tNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\\n   165\\tto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\\n   166\\tinstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\\n   167\\tfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\\n   168\\tconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\\n   169\\tmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\\n   170\\tstep of the source proof.\\n   171\\t\\n   172\\tFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\\n   173\\t\\n   174\\t- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\\n   175\\t- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\\n   176\\t- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n   177\\t  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n   178\\t\\n   179\\t---\\n   180\\t\\n   181\\t## Warnings\\n   182\\t\\n   183\\tThese should be flagged for review but may be acceptable with justification.\\n   184\\t\\n   185\\t### Placeholder tactics\\n   186\\t\\n   187\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n   188\\t|---------|------|\\n   189\\t| `exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`, `suggest` | Search tactics left as placeholders — replace with the concrete result |\\n   190\\t\\n   191\\t### Safety / termination bypasses\\n   192\\t\\n   193\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n   194\\t|---------|------|\\n   195\\t| `unsafe def` | Bypasses Lean safety checks; should not appear in proof-relevant code |\\n   196\\t| `partial def` | No termination proof required; unsound if used to build proof terms |\\n   197\\t| `implemented_by` / `implementedBy` | Decouples runtime behavior from proven specification |\\n   198\\t\\n   199\\t### Suspicious options\\n   200\\t\\n   201\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n   202\\t|---------|------|\\n   203\\t| `set_option maxHeartbeats 0` | Disables timeout — can hide non-terminating proofs |\\n   204\\t| `set_option maxHeartbeats` with values >= 4,000,000 | 20x the default (200,000) — likely indicates an inefficient proof |\\n   205\\t| `set_option maxRecDepth` with values >= 10,000 | May hide structural issues in proofs |\\n   206\\t\\n   207\\t### Debug artifacts\\n   208\\t\\n   209\\t| Pattern | Risk |\\n   210\\t|---------|------|\\n   211\\t| `dbg_trace` | Debug trace left in code |\\n   212\\t| `stop` | Halts elaboration — development aid only |\\n   213\\t| `#check`, `#eval`, `#print` in proof files | Debug commands that should be removed |\\n   214\\t\\n   215\\t---\\n   216\\t\\n   217\\t## How to use this file\\n   218\\t\\n   219\\t**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\\n   220\\t[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\\n   221\\tproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\\n   222\\tstructure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why\\n   223\\tconditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a\\n   224\\ttracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.\\n   225\\t\\n   226\\t**In CI review prompts**: Reference this file instead of inlining the rules:\\n   227\\t```\\n   228\\tRead `docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md` for the complete list of proof integrity\\n   229\\trules. Flag blockers as must-fix issues that should block merge.\\n   230\\tFlag warnings as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be\\n   231\\tacceptable with justification.\\n   232\\t```\\n   233\\t\\n   234\\t**For manual review**: Use this as a checklist when reviewing Lean PRs.\\n   235\\t\\n   236\\t**Updating rules**: Edit this file and all referencing workflows will\\n   237\\tautomatically pick up the changes.\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n36024:+{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_35\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"nl -ba docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex | sed -n '1,340p'\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"     1\\t\\\\documentclass[11pt]{article}\\n     2\\t\\n     3\\t\\\\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}\\n     4\\t\\\\usepackage{xurl}\\n     5\\t\\\\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}\\n     6\\t\\\\setlength{\\\\emergencystretch}{2em}\\n     7\\t\\n     8\\t\\\\input{command}\\n     9\\t\\n    10\\t\\\\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}\\n    11\\t\\\\author{}\\n    12\\t\\\\date{2026-04-29}\\n    13\\t\\n    14\\t\\\\begin{document}\\n    15\\t\\\\maketitle\\n    16\\t\\n    17\\t\\\\section{Purpose}\\n    18\\t\\n    19\\tWhen a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source\\n    20\\tshould remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,\\n    21\\tmissing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical\\n    22\\tdiscrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.\\n    23\\tIn this repository such notes live under \\\\path{docs/paper-gaps/}. The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary\\n   107\\tmathematics.\\n   108\\t\\n   109\\tSometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:\\n   110\\tthe formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an\\n   111\\texisting library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.\\n   112\\tThese are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes. theorem eq_comm_eq {α : Sort*} (a b : α) : (a = b) = (b = a) := by rw [@eq_comm _ a b]
theorem iff_comm_eq (a b : Prop) : (a ↔ b) = (b ↔ a) := by rw [@iff_comm a b]

/-- On a goal of the form of `x = y`, also try to simplify `y = x`.

If simplifying `y = x` gives `y' = x'` then this simproc returns `x' = y'` (so that the use of
commutativity is transparent), otherwise it returns the result of simplifying `y = x` unmodified.
-/
simproc_decl eqComm (_ = _) := fun e => do
  let_expr Eq _ x y := e | return .continue
  let symmExpr ← mkEq y x
  let r ← withoutTheorems #[`eqComm,
    -- These theorems would cause an infinite loop:
    ``eq_comm, ``Bool.not_eq_eq_eq_not, `inv_eq_iff_eq_inv, `eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq,
    `eq_mul_inv_iff_mul_eq, `neg_eq_iff_eq_neg, `Function.Involutive.eq_iff,
    `vadd_eq_iff_eq_neg_vadd, `Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply,
    -- These theorems aren't commute-resistant (they turn an equality into a non-equality in a
    -- non-commutative way.)
    ``beq_iff_eq, ``funext_iff, ``eq_iff_iff, `Prod.swap_eq_iff_eq_swap, ``left_eq_dite_iff,
    ``right_eq_dite_iff] do
    withTraceNode `Meta.Tactic.simp (fun _ => return m!"commuting equality: {e}") <| simp symmExpr
  -- If no actual progress happened (modulo commutativity), return early.
  match_expr r.expr with
  | Eq _ y' x' =>
    if (y' == y && x' == x) || (y' == x && x' == y) then do
      return .continue none
  | _ => pure ()
  let symmR ← Result.mkEqTrans { expr := symmExpr, proof? := ← mkAppM ``eq_comm_eq #[x, y] } r
  -- If we started with `x = y`, and the result of simplifying `y = x` was `y' = x'`, then we want
  -- to end up with `x' = y'`.
  match_expr r.expr with
  | Eq _ y' x' =>
    return .visit (← symmR.mkEqTrans
      { expr := ← mkEq x' y', proof? := ← mkAppM ``eq_comm_eq #[y', x'] })
  | _ => return .done symmR

/-- On a goal of the form of `x ↔ y`, also try to simplify `y ↔ x`.

If simplifying `y ↔ x` gives `y' ↔ x'` then this simproc returns `x' ↔ y'` (so that the use of
commutativity is transparent), otherwise it returns the result of simplifying `y ↔ x` unmodified.
-/
simproc_decl iffComm (_ ↔ _) := fun e => do
  let_expr Iff x y := e | return .continue
  let symmExpr := .app (.app (.const ``Iff []) y) x
  let r ← withoutTheorems #[`iffComm,
      -- These theorems would cause an infinite loop:
      ``Iff.comm,
      -- These theorems aren't commute-resistant (they turn an iff into a non-iff in a
      -- non-commutative way).
      ``and_congr_left_iff, ``and_congr_right_iff,  ``iff_def, ``iff_def',
      ``iff_iff_implies_and_implies, ``Bool.coe_iff_coe] do
    withTraceNode `Meta.Tactic.simp (fun _ => return m!"commuting iff: {e}") <| simp symmExpr
  -- If no actual progress happened (modulo commutativity), return early.
  if r.expr == symmExpr || r.expr == e then return .continue
  let symmR ← Result.mkEqTrans { expr := symmExpr, proof? := ← mkAppM ``iff_comm_eq #[x, y] } r
  -- If we started with `x ↔ y`, and the result of simplifying `y ↔ x` was `y' ↔ x'`, then we want
  -- to end up with `x' ↔ y'`.
  match_expr r.expr with
  | Iff y' x' =>
    return .visit (← symmR.mkEqTrans
      { expr := .app (.app (.const ``Iff []) x') y', proof? := ← mkAppM ``iff_comm_eq #[y', x'] })
  | _ => return .done symmR

end CommSimproc

/-- Wrapper for adding elementary propositions to the type class systems.
Warning: this can easily be abused. See the rest of this docstring for details.

Certain propositions should not be treated as a class globally,
but sometimes it is very convenient to be able to use the type class system
in specific circumstances.

For example, `ZMod p` is a field if and only if `p` is a prime number.
In order to be able to find this field instance automatically by type class search,
we have to turn `p.Prime` into an instance implicit assumption.

On the other hand, making `Nat.Prime` a class would require a major refactoring of the library,
and it is questionable whether making `Nat.Prime` a class is desirable at all.
The compromise is to add the assumption `[Fact p.Prime]` to `ZMod.instField`.

In particular, this class is not intended for turning the type class system
into an automated theorem prover for first-order logic. -/
class Fact (p : Prop) : Prop where
  /-- `Fact.out` contains the unwrapped witness for the fact represented by the instance of
  `Fact p`. -/
  out : p

library_note «fact non-instances» /--
In most cases, we should not have global instances of `Fact`; typeclass search is not an
advanced proof search engine, and adding any such instance has the potential to cause
slowdowns everywhere. We instead declare them as lemmata and make them local instances as required.
-/

theorem Fact.elim {p : Prop} (h : Fact p) : p := h.1
theorem fact_iff {p : Prop} : Fact p ↔ p := ⟨fun h ↦ h.1, fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩⟩

instance {p : Prop} [Decidable p] : Decidable (Fact p) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ fact_iff.symm

/-!
# The directly indexed low-degree game

This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
for the directly indexed low-degree interface.

## References

The underlying game is blueprint
`def:ld-game`, with source origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
direct scalar field. -/
abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D

/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
      evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
value is used as a fallback. -/
noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D

/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
  | .aline, sample =>
      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
  | .dline, sample =>
      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩

/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))

/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _

/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))

/-- The canonical code equivalence for `DirectLdAnswer`, sending point,
axis-line, and diagonal-line answers to the three summands. -/
noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
  toFun
    | .pointVals a => .inl a
    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
  invFun
    | .inl a => .pointVals a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro answer
    rcases answer with a | a
    · rfl
    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl

instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩

noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm

+/-"'!
+# Compact classical low individual degree game
+
+This Mathlib-only module gives the concrete product-space presentation of the
+classical low individual degree game used by the Palomar statement surface.
+It keeps the complete ambient question carrier and the three answer summands,
+including malformed answers that the verifier rejects.
+
+The final statement module instantiates `K` with the carrier of the existing
+`MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel`.  Its copied dependency contract consists of
+`MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAdmissibleSize`,
+`MIPStarRE.QPBT.FixedFieldModel`, and that single registered selector.
+
+## References
+
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-440`.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar
+
+/-- The numerical domain of the classical low individual degree game. -/
+structure LowDegreeParams where
+  q : ℕ
+  m : ℕ
+  d : ℕ
+  k : ℕ
+  hm : 1 ≤ m
+  hd : 1 ≤ d
+  hk : 1 ≤ k
+  hq : ∃ r : ℕ, Odd r ∧ q = 2 ''^ r
+  hdvd : m ∣ q
+
+/-- The positive dimension supplies the nonzero modulus used by `chiIndex`. -/
+instance LowDegreeParams.instNeZeroM (P : LowDegreeParams) : NeZero P.m :=
+  ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
+
+/-- The three question types of the classical low individual degree game. -/
+inductive LowDegreeType where
+  | point
+  | aline
+  | dline
+  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype, Inhabited
+
+/-- The full point, seed, and direction space sampled by the verifier. -/
+abbrev LowDegreeSpace (P : LowDegreeParams) (K : Type) :=
+  ((Fin P.m → K) × K) × (Fin P.m → K)
+
+/-- A typed low-degree question, retaining every ambient coordinate. -/
+abbrev LowDegreeQuestion (P : LowDegreeParams) (K : Type) :=
+  LowDegreeType × LowDegreeSpace P K
+
+/-- The full three-summand answer alphabet, including malformed answers. -/
+abbrev LowDegreeAnswer (P : LowDegreeParams) (K : Type) :=
+  (Fin P.k → K) ⊕
+    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → K) ⊕
+      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → K))
+
+/-- Simultaneous bounded polynomial representatives used by low-degree soundness. -/
+noncomputable abbrev LowDegreePolynomialTuple (P : LowDegreeParams) (K : Type)
+    [CommSemiring K] :=
+  Fin P.k → ↥(MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin P.m) K P.d)
+
+/-- Restricted-degree polynomials over a finite semiring form a finite type. -/
+noncomputable instance restrictedDegreeFintype (m d : ℕ) (K : Type)
+    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] :
+    Fintype ↥(MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d) := by
+  letI : Finite ↥(MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d) :=
+    Module.finite_of_finite K
+  exact Fintype.ofFinite _
+
+/-- The least coordinate at which a nonzero direction is nonzero. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreePivot {K : Type} [Zero K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
+    (v : Fin m → K) (hv : v ≠ 0) : Fin m := by
+  let support := Finset.univ.filter fun j => v j ≠ 0
+  exact support.min'"' (by
+    by_contra h
+    apply hv
+    funext j
+    simpa only [Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff,
+      Finset.mem_univ, true_implies] using congrFun (show support = ∅ from h) j)
+
+/-- The elementary least-pivot representative, with identity at zero direction. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeLineRep {K : Type} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
+    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
+  if hv : v = 0 then u
+  else
+    let j := lowDegreePivot v hv
+    u - (u j / v j) • v
+
+/-- The paper's balanced seed-to-coordinate map. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeChiIndex {K : Type} (P : LowDegreeParams)
+    (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) (s : K) : Fin P.m :=
+  Fin.ofNat P.m ((encoding s).val / (P.q / P.m))
+
+/-- Zero the direction coordinates preceding "'`i`. -/
+def lowDegreePrefix {K : Type} [Zero K] {m : ℕ} (i : Fin m) (v : Fin m → K) :
+    Fin m → K :=
+  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
+
+/-- The concrete question map for each of the three question types. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeMap {K : Type} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
+    (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    LowDegreeType → LowDegreeSpace P K → LowDegreeSpace P K
+  | .point, z => ((z.1.1, 0), 0)
+  | .aline, z =>
+      let direction := Pi.single (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding z.1.2) 1
+      ((lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1 direction, z.1.2), 0)
+  | .dline, z =>
+      let direction := lowDegreePrefix (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding z.1.2) z.2
+      ((lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1 direction, z.1.2), direction)
+
+/-- The uniform law on all nine ordered type pairs and the entire ambient space. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeQuestionPMF {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
+    [DecidableEq K] (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    PMF (LowDegreeQuestion P K × LowDegreeQuestion P K) :=
+  (PMF.uniformOfFintype ((LowDegreeType × LowDegreeType) × LowDegreeSpace P K)).map
+    fun z => ((z.1.1, lowDegreeMap P encoding z.1.1 z.2),
+      (z.1.2, lowDegreeMap P encoding z.1.2 z.2))
+
+/-- Evaluate a bounded coefficient list at a field element. -/
+def lowDegreeEval {K : Type} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
+  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ''^ i.val
+
+/-- Whether an answer lies in the summand prescribed by its question type. -/
+def validLowDegreeAnswer {P : LowDegreeParams} {K : Type} :
+    LowDegreeType → LowDegreeAnswer P K → Bool
+  | .point, .inl _ => true
+  | .aline, .inr (.inl _) => true
+  | .dline, .inr (.inr _) => true
+  | _, _ => false
+
+/-- The complete low-degree verifier, including universal zero-direction tests. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeWin {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
+    (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    LowDegreeQuestion P K → LowDegreeQuestion P K →
+      LowDegreeAnswer P K → LowDegreeAnswer P K → Bool :=
+  open Classical in
+  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
+    if validLowDegreeAnswer tA a && validLowDegreeAnswer tB b then
+      match tA, tB, a, b with
+      | .point, .point, .inl u, .inl v => decide (u = v)
+      | .aline, .point, .inr (.inl f), .inl u => decide (∀ t,
+          xB.1.1 = xA.1.1 + t • Pi.single (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding xA.1.2) 1 →
+            ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)
+      | .point, .aline, .inl u, .inr (.inl f) => decide (∀ t,
+          xA.1.1 = xB.1.1 + t • Pi.single (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding xB.1.2) 1 →
+            ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)
+      | .dline, .point, .inr (.inr f), .inl u => decide (∀ t,
+          xB.1.1 = xA.1.1 + t • xA.2 → ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)
+      | .point, .dline, .inl u, .inr (.inr f) => decide (∀ t,
+          xA.1.1 = xB.1.1 + t • xB.2 → ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)
+      | .aline, .aline, .inr (.inl f), .inr (.inl g) => decide (f = g)
+      | .dline, .dline, .inr (.inr f), .inr (.inr g) => decide (f = g)
+      | _, _, _, _ => true
+    else false
+
+/-- The compact classical low individual degree game. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeGame {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
+    (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    Game (LowDegreeQuestion P K) (LowDegreeQuestion P K)
+      (LowDegreeAnswer P K) (LowDegreeAnswer P K) where
+  μ := lowDegreeQuestionPMF P encoding
+  decide := lowDegreeWin P encoding
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar
*** End Patch

+  letI : Finite ↥(MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d) :=
+    Module.finite_of_finite K
+  exact Fintype.ofFinite _

+    by_contra h

+    funext j

+noncomputable def lowDegreeLineRep {K : Type} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
+    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
+  if hv : v = 0 then u
+  else
+    let j := lowDegreePivot v hv
+    u - (u j / v j) • v

+noncomputable def lowDegreeChiIndex {K : Type} (P : LowDegreeParams)
+    (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) (s : K) : Fin P.m :=
+  Fin.ofNat P.m ((encoding s).val / (P.q / P.m))
+
+/-- Zero the direction coordinates preceding "'`i`. -/

+    Fin m → K :=
+  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j

+noncomputable def lowDegreeMap {K : Type} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
+    (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    LowDegreeType → LowDegreeSpace P K → LowDegreeSpace P K
+  | .point, z => ((z.1.1, 0), 0)
+  | .aline, z =>
+      let direction := Pi.single (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding z.1.2) 1
+      ((lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1 direction, z.1.2), 0)
+  | .dline, z =>
+      let direction := lowDegreePrefix (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding z.1.2) z.2
+      ((lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1 direction, z.1.2), direction)
+
+/-- The uniform law on all nine ordered type pairs and the entire ambient space. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeQuestionPMF {K : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K]
+    [DecidableEq K] (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :
+    PMF (LowDegreeQuestion P K × LowDegreeQuestion P K) :=
+  (PMF.uniformOfFintype ((LowDegreeType × LowDegreeType) × LowDegreeSpace P K)).map

+  | _, _ => false

+          xA.1.1 = xB.1.1 + t • Pi.single (lowDegreeChiIndex P encoding xB.1.2) 1 →
+            ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)
+      | .dline, .point, .inr (.inr f), .inl u => decide (∀ t,
+          xB.1.1 = xA.1.1 + t • xA.2 → ∀ j, lowDegreeEval (f j) t = u j)

+    (P : LowDegreeParams) (encoding : K ≃ Fin P.q) :

+  decide := lowDegreeWin P encoding

+/-"'!
+# Exact bridge for the compact low individual degree game
+
+This module identifies the compact product-space game with the existing
+low-degree game.  The bridge is by explicit equivalences of question
+coordinates and answer summands.  It preserves the question PMF, every branch
+of the Boolean verifier, and the value of every compact strategy exactly.
+
+## References
+
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-440`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+/-- Copy the original numerical parameter record into the compact domain. -/
+def LowDegreeParams.ofLdParams (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) : LowDegreeParams where
+  q := P.q
+  m := P.m
+  d := P.d
+  k := P.k
+  hm := P.hm
+  hd := P.hd
+  hk := P.hk
+  hq := P.hq
+  hdvd := P.hdvd
+
+/-- The compact and original three-element question-type carriers are equivalent. -/
+def lowDegreeTypeEquiv : LowDegreeType ≃ MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType where
+  toFun
+    | .point => .point
+    | .aline => .aline
+    | .dline => .dline
+  invFun
+    | .point => .point
+    | .aline => .aline
+    | .dline => .dline
+  left_inv t := by cases t <;> rfl
+  right_inv t := by cases t <;> rfl
+
+/-- Split-function coordinates identify the complete compact and original spaces. -/
+def lowDegreeSpaceEquiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) ≃
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace P :=
+  (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldSpaceSplit P).symm
+
+/-- Typed questions are equivalent by the explicit type and coordinate maps. -/
+def lowDegreeQuestionEquiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    LowDegreeQuestion P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) ≃
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdQuestion P :=
+  Equiv.prodCongr lowDegreeTypeEquiv (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P)
+
+/-- The three answer summands are exactly the original answer constructors. -/
+noncomputable def lowDegreeAnswerEquiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    LowDegreeAnswer P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) ≃
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdAnswer P :=
+  (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
+
+/-- The complete common-source spaces are equivalent coordinate by coordinate. -/
+def lowDegreeSourceEquiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    ((LowDegreeType × LowDegreeType) ×
+        LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) ≃
+      ((MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType × MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType) ×
+        MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace P) :=
+  Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.prodCongr lowDegreeTypeEquiv lowDegreeTypeEquiv)
+    (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P)
+
+/-- Equivalence of the two ordered question-pair carriers. -/
+def lowDegreeQuestionPairEquiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    (LowDegreeQuestion P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) ×
+        LowDegreeQuestion P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) ≃
+      (MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdQuestion P × MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdQuestion P) :=
+  Equiv.prodCongr (lowDegreeQuestionEquiv P) (lowDegreeQuestionEquiv P)
+
+/-- The compact seed-index map is the original `chiIndex`. -/
+@[simp] theorem lowDegreeChiIndex_eq (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (s : MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) :
+    lowDegreeChiIndex P.ofLdParams
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model) s =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P s := by
+  rfl
+
+/-- The compact prefix projection is the original prefix projection. -/
+@[simp] theorem lowDegreePrefix_eq (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) :
+    lowDegreePrefix i v = MIPStarRE.QPBT.prefixProjection i v :=
+  rfl
+
+/-- The compact least nonzero coordinate is the one used by the published formula. -/
+theorem lowDegreePivot_eq_linePivotIndex {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
+    [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) (hv : v ≠ 0) :
+    lowDegreePivot v hv = MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePivotIndex v hv := by
+  rfl
+
+/-- The compact elementary representative is exactly the canonical representative. -/
+theorem lowDegreeLineRep_eq_lineRepMap {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
+    [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (u v : Fin m → K) :
+    lowDegreeLineRep u v = MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap v u := by
+  rw [MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap_apply_eq_explicitLineRep]
+  simp only [lowDegreeLineRep, MIPStarRE.QPBT.explicitLineRep]
+  split_ifs with hv
+  · rfl
+  · rw [lowDegreePivot_eq_linePivotIndex v hv]
+
+/-- The compact point map agrees with the original point map. -/
+theorem lowDegreeMap_point_equiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (z : LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) :
+    lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P
+        (lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
+          .point z) =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldPointCL P (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P z) := by
+  rfl
+
+/-- The compact axis-line map agrees with the original axis-line map. -/
+theorem lowDegreeMap_aline_equiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (z : LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) :
+    lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P
+        (lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
+          .aline z) =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldALineCL P (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P z) := by
+  funext i
+  rcases i with (j | u) | j
+  · change lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1
+        (Pi.single (MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P z.1.2) 1) j =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection (MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P z.1.2))
+        z.1.1 j
+    rw [lowDegreeLineRep_eq_lineRepMap]
+    rfl
+  · cases u
+    rfl
+  · rfl
+
+/-- The compact diagonal-line map agrees with the original diagonal-line map. -/
+theorem lowDegreeMap_dline_equiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (z : LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) :
+    lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P
+        (lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)
+          .dline z) =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldDLineCL P (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P z) := by
+  funext i
+  rcases i with (j | u) | j
+  · change lowDegreeLineRep z.1.1
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.prefixProjection
+          (MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P z.1.2) z.2) j =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.lineRepMap
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.prefixProjection
+          (MIPStarRE.QPBT.chiIndex P z.1.2) z.2) z.1.1 j
+    rw [lowDegreeLineRep_eq_lineRepMap]
+  · cases u
+    rfl
+  · rfl
+
+/-- All three compact question maps commute with the coordinate equivalence. -/
+theorem lowDegreeMap_equiv (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams)
+    (t : LowDegreeType)
+    (z : LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P)) :
+    lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P
+        (lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model) t z) =
+      MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldCL P (lowDegreeTypeEquiv t) (lowDegreeSpaceEquiv P z) := by
+  cases t with
+  | point => exact lowDegreeMap_point_equiv P z
+  | aline => exact lowDegreeMap_aline_equiv P z
+  | dline => exact lowDegreeMap_dline_equiv P z
+
+/-- The compact question PMF is exactly the original question distribution. -/
+theorem lowDegreeQuestionPMF_map (P : MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdParams) :
+    (lowDegreeQuestionPMF P.ofLdParams
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model)).map
+        (lowDegreeQuestionPairEquiv P) =
+      (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldGame P).μ.toPMF (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldGame P).μ_prob := by
+  let compactMap := fun z :
+      (LowDegreeType × LowDegreeType) ×
+        LowDegreeSpace P.ofLdParams (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ScalarQ P) =>
+    ((z.1.1, lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model) z.1.1 z.2),
+      (z.1.2, lowDegreeMap P.ofLdParams
+        (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model) z.1.2 z.2))
+  let originalMap := fun z :
+      (MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType × MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdType) ×
+        MIPStarRE.QPBT.LdSpace P =>
+    ((z.1.1, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldCL P z.1.1 z.2),
+      (z.1.2, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldCL P z.1.2 z.2))
+  have hcomm : lowDegreeQuestionPairEquiv P ∘ compactMap =
+      originalMap ∘ lowDegreeSourceEquiv P := by
+    funext z
+    apply Prod.ext
+    · apply Prod.ext
+      · rfl
+      · exact lowDegreeMap_equiv P z.1.1 z.2
+    · apply Prod.ext
+      · rfl
+      · exact lowDegreeMap_equiv P z.1.2 z.2
+  rw [show lowDegreeQuestionPMF P.ofLdParams
+      (MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryRepresentation P.model) =
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype _).map compactMap by rfl]
+  rw [PMF.map_comp, hcomm, ← PMF.map_comp]
+  rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv (lowDegreeSourceEquiv P)]
+  rw [PMF.map_comp]
+  change (PMF.uniformOfFintype _).map originalMap =
+    (MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldQuestionDistribution P).toPMF _
+  rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution.toPMF_map]
+  rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.uniformDistribution_toPMF]
+
+/-- Polynomial coefficient evaluation is unchanged by the compact presentation. -/
+@[simp] theorem lowDegreeEval_eq_evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
+    {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) :
+    lowDegreeEval c t = MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient c t :=
+  rfl

+  rcases y with ⟨tB, xB⟩

+  · rcases b with b | b

+          MIPStarRE.QPBT.validLdAnswer, lowDegreeQuestionEquiv,
+          lowDegreeTypeEquiv, lowDegreeSpaceEquiv, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldSpaceSplit,
+          lowDegreeAnswerEquiv, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldAnswerEquiv,
+          MIPStarRE.QPBT.alinePointCondition, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dlinePointCondition,
+          lowDegreeEval, MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient,
+          MIPStarRE.QPBT.coordinateDirection]
+    · rcases b with b | b <;> cases tA <;> cases tB <;>
+        simp [lowDegreeWin, validLowDegreeAnswer, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldWinPredicate,
+          MIPStarRE.QPBT.validLdAnswer, lowDegreeQuestionEquiv,
+          lowDegreeTypeEquiv, lowDegreeSpaceEquiv, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldSpaceSplit,
+          lowDegreeAnswerEquiv, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldAnswerEquiv,
+          MIPStarRE.QPBT.alinePointCondition, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dlinePointCondition,
+          lowDegreeEval, MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient,

+  · rcases a with a | a

module

public import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Palomar.Foundation

/-!
# Compact classical low individual degree game

This Mathlib-only module gives the concrete product-space presentation of the
classical low individual degree game used by the Palomar statement surface.
It keeps the complete ambient question carrier and the three answer summands,
including malformed answers that the verifier rejects.

The final statement module instantiates `K` with the carrier of the existing
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.fixedFieldModel`.  Its copied dependency contract consists of
`MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAdmissibleSize`,
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.FixedFieldModel`, and that single registered selector.
